title.zh: 卷459 列傳二百四十六 冯子材 王孝祺 陈嘉 蒋宗汉 苏元春 马盛治 王德榜 张春發 萧得龙 马维骐 覃修纲 吴永安 孙开华 朱焕明 苏得胜 章高元 欧阳利见
title.en: Volume 459 Biographies 246: Feng Zicai, Wang Xiaoqi, Chen Jia, Jiang Zonghan, Su Yuanchun, Ma Shengzhi, Wang Debang, Zhang Chunfa, Xiao Delong, Ma Weiqi, Tan Xiu Gang, Wu Yongan, Sun Kaihua, Zhu Huanming, Su Desheng, Zhang Gaoyuan, Ou Yanglijian
title.raw: 卷459 列傳二百四十六 冯子材 王孝祺 陈嘉 蒋宗汉 苏元春 马盛治 王德榜 张春發 萧得龙 马维骐 覃修纲 吴永安 孙开华 朱焕明 苏得胜 章高元 欧阳利见

sentences.zh: 馮子材，字翠亭，廣東欽州人。

translations.literal: Feng Zicai, style name Cuiting, was a native of Qinzhou in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zicai, courtesy name Cuiting, came from Qinzhou in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 初從向榮討粵寇，補千總。

translations.literal: At first he followed Xiang Rong in campaigning against the Cantonese rebels and was appointed a company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Xiang Rong against the Cantonese rebels and received appointment as a company commander.

sentences.zh: 平博白，賜號色爾固楞巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When Bobai was pacified, he was granted the title Se'erguleng Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Bobai, he was awarded the Manchu heroic title Se'erguleng Batulu.

sentences.zh: 改隸張國樑麾下，從克鎮江、丹陽，嘗一日夷寇壘七十餘。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve under Zhang Guoliang, took part in capturing Zhenjiang and Danyang, and on one day destroyed more than seventy rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned to Zhang Guoliang's command, he helped take Zhenjiang and Danyang and once in a single day leveled more than seventy rebel forts.

sentences.zh: 國樑拊其背曰：「子勇，餘愧弗如！

translations.literal: Guoliang clapped him on the back and said: "You are brave; I am not your equal!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang slapped his back and said, "Son, you are valiant—I cannot match you!"

sentences.zh: 」積勳至副將。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he rose to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: By accumulated merit he advanced to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 國樑歿，代領其眾。

translations.literal: When Guoliang died, he took command of his forces in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: After Guoliang died, he succeeded to command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 取溧水，擢總兵。

translations.literal: He captured Lishui and was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took Lishui and was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 同治初，將三千人守鎮江。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign he led three thousand men to defend Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi era he garrisoned Zhenjiang with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 時江北諸將多自置卡榷釐稅，子材曰：「此何與武人事？

translations.literal: At that time many generals north of the Yangtze set up their own checkpoint stations to levy taxes. Zicai said: "What has this to do with military men?"
translations.idiomatic: Many Yangtze-north commanders then ran private toll stations and levies. Feng said, "What business is that of soldiers?"

sentences.zh: 」請曾國籓遣官司之。

translations.literal: He asked Zeng Guofan to send officials to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Zeng Guofan to send civil officials to take charge of them.

sentences.zh: 所部可二萬，餉恆詘，無怨言。

translations.literal: His command numbered about twenty thousand; pay was constantly short, yet there were no complaints.
translations.idiomatic: His force numbered some twenty thousand; rations were chronically short, yet no one grumbled.

sentences.zh: 蒞鎮六載，待士有紀綱，士亦樂為所用。

translations.literal: During six years at the garrison he maintained discipline among the troops, and the troops were glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: For six years at the post he kept strict order among his men, and they were glad to follow him.

sentences.zh: 寇攻百餘次，卒堅不可拔。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked more than a hundred times, yet in the end the city stood firm and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels assaulted the place over a hundred times, yet it held and could not be stormed.

sentences.zh: 事寧，擢廣西提督，賞黃馬褂，予世職。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was promoted to military governor of Guangxi, rewarded with a yellow riding jacket, and granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: After peace returned he was made military governor of Guangxi, given a yellow riding jacket, and granted a hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 赴粵平羅肅，移師討黔苗，克全茗、感墟。

translations.literal: He went to Guangdong to pacify Luo Su, then moved his army to campaign against the Miao in Guizhou and captured Quanming and Ganxu.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Guangdong to suppress Luo Su, then marched against the Guizhou Miao and took Quanming and Ganxu.

sentences.zh: 九年，出鎮南關，攻克安邊、河陽，凱旋，再予世職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he marched out from Zhennan Pass, captured Anbian and Heyang, returned in triumph, and was again granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he advanced from Zhennan Pass, took Anbian and Heyang, returned victorious, and received a second hereditary grant.

sentences.zh: 光緒改元，赴貴州提督任。

translations.literal: When the Guangxu reign began, he took up the post of military governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangxu reign he assumed the Guizhou governorship.

sentences.zh: 七年，還廣西。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he returned to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he returned to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，稱疾歸。

translations.literal: The next year he pleaded illness and retired.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 越二年，法越事作，張樹聲蘄其治團練，遣使往趣駕。

translations.literal: Two years later the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose; Zhang Shusheng begged him to organize local militia and sent an envoy to urge him to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on, as the Franco-Vietnamese crisis broke out, Zhang Shusheng asked him to organize militia and sent a messenger to summon him.

sentences.zh: 比至，子材方短衣赤足、攜童叱犢歸，啟來意，卻之。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, Zicai was just returning in short coat and bare feet, driving an ox with a boy, and when he learned the purpose he declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the messenger arrived, Feng was coming home barefoot in a short coat, driving cattle with a boy; hearing the errand, he refused.

sentences.zh: 已，聞樹聲賢，詣廣州。

translations.literal: Later, hearing that Shusheng was worthy, he went to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, learning that Shusheng was a man of merit, he went to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 適張之洞至，禮事之，請總前敵師幹衛粵、桂。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong happened to arrive, treated him with ceremony, and asked him to command the front-line staff guarding Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong had just arrived, honored him, and asked him to take overall charge of the forward staff defending Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，朝命佐廣西邊外軍事。

translations.literal: After more than a year the court ordered him to assist in frontier military affairs in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the court ordered him to assist in Guangxi border warfare.

sentences.zh: 其時蘇元春為督辦，子材以其新進出己右，恆悒悒。

translations.literal: At that time Su Yuanchun was superintendent; Zicai, because Yuanchun was newly advanced and ranked above him, was constantly discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yuanchun then held the superintendency; Feng, resenting that the newcomer outranked him, was often ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 聞諒山警，亟赴鎮南關，而法軍已焚關退。

translations.literal: Hearing the alarm from Lang Son, he hastened to Zhennan Pass, but the French army had already burned the pass and withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: On news of danger at Lang Son he rushed to Zhennan Pass, only to find the French had burned the pass and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 龍州危棘，子材以關前隘跨東西兩嶺，備險奧，乃令築長牆，萃所部扼守，遣王孝祺勤軍軍其後為犄角。

translations.literal: Longzhou was in peril; Zicai saw that the pass before the gate straddled two ridges east and west, with formidable terrain, so he ordered a long wall built, concentrated his troops to hold it, and sent Wang Xiaoqi's Qin Army to camp behind as a supporting angle.
translations.idiomatic: With Longzhou threatened, Feng saw the pass before the gate spanning two ridges with formidable ground; he had a long wall built, massed his troops to hold it, and posted Wang Xiaoqi's Qin Army in the rear as a reserve wing.

sentences.zh: 敵聲某日攻關，子材逆料其先期至，乃決先發製敵。

translations.literal: The enemy announced they would attack the pass on a certain day; Zicai anticipated they would come early and resolved to strike first and seize the initiative.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy said they would assault the pass on a set day; Feng expected them early and decided to strike first.

sentences.zh: 潘鼎新止之，群議亦不欲戰。

translations.literal: Pan Dingxin stopped him, and the assembled opinion also did not wish to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Dingxin restrained him, and the council likewise opposed battle.

sentences.zh: 子材力爭，親率勤軍襲文淵，於是三至關外矣。

translations.literal: Zicai argued forcefully, personally led the Qin Army in a raid on Van Tien—thus for the third time he reached beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Feng insisted, led the Qin Army himself to raid Van Tien, and for the third time stood outside the pass.

sentences.zh: 宵薄敵壘，斬虜多。

translations.literal: At night they pressed the enemy stockades and killed many captives.
translations.idiomatic: By night they closed on the enemy camps and killed many.

sentences.zh: 法悉眾分三路入，子材語將士曰：「法軍再入關，何顏見粵民？

translations.literal: The French committed their full strength and entered by three routes; Zicai told the officers and men: "If the French enter the pass again, how can we face the people of Guangdong?"
translations.idiomatic: The French brought their full strength in three columns; Feng told his troops, "If the French enter the pass again, what face have we to show the people of Guangdong?"

sentences.zh: 必死拒之！

translations.literal: We must die resisting them!
translations.idiomatic: We must die holding them!

sentences.zh: 」士氣皆奮。

translations.literal: Morale was everywhere roused.
translations.idiomatic: Every man's spirit rose.

sentences.zh: 法軍攻長牆亟，次黑兵，次教匪，砲聲震山谷，槍彈積陣前厚寸許。

translations.literal: The French army pressed the long wall fiercely; next came the black troops, then the Catholic auxiliaries; cannon shook the valleys, and bullets piled before the line a finger's thickness deep.
translations.idiomatic: The French hammered the long wall; African troops followed, then Catholic auxiliaries; guns shook the hills and spent balls heaped a finger deep before the line.

sentences.zh: 與諸軍痛擊，敵稍卻。

translations.literal: Together with the other armies they struck hard, and the enemy fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: With the allied forces they struck hard and the enemy gave ground.

sentences.zh: 越日復湧至，子材居中，元春為承，孝祺將右，陳嘉、蔣宗漢將左。

translations.literal: The next day they surged up again; Zicai stood in the center, Yuanchun supported him, Xiaoqi commanded the right, and Chen Jia and Jiang Zonghan the left.
translations.idiomatic: Next day they surged forward again; Feng held the center, Yuanchun the reserve, Xiaoqi the right, Chen Jia and Jiang Zonghan the left.

sentences.zh: 子材指麾諸將使屹立，遇退後者刃之。

translations.literal: Zicai directed the generals to stand firm and executed any who fell back.
translations.idiomatic: Feng ordered the generals to hold their ground and killed any who retreated.

sentences.zh: 自開壁持矛大呼，率二子相榮、相華躍出搏戰。

translations.literal: He himself opened the wall, spear in hand, shouting loudly, and led his two sons Xiangrong and Xianghua leaping out to grapple with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the breastwork, spear raised, shouting, and led his sons Xiangrong and Xianghua leaping out to fight hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 諸軍以子材年七十，奮身陷陣，皆感奮，殊死鬥。

translations.literal: The armies, seeing that Zicai at seventy was throwing himself into the battle, were all stirred and fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Feng at seventy charge into the fray, every unit was stirred to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 關外游勇客民亦助戰，斬法將數十人，追至關外二十里而還。

translations.literal: Mercenaries and resident civilians beyond the pass also joined the fight; dozens of French officers were killed, and they pursued twenty li beyond the pass before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Irregulars and settlers outside the pass joined in; dozens of French officers were cut down, and the pursuit ran twenty li beyond the pass before they turned back.

sentences.zh: 越二日，克文淵，被賞賚。

translations.literal: Two days later Van Tien was taken and rewards were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Two days on they took Van Tien and received imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 連复諒城、長慶，擒斬三畫、五畫兵總各一，乘勝規拉木，悉返侵地。

translations.literal: They successively recovered Lang Son and Changqing, captured and beheaded one company commander each of the three-stripe and five-stripe ranks, pressed the advantage toward Lam, and wholly restored the invaded territory.
translations.idiomatic: They retook Lang Son and Changqing, killed one three-stripe and one five-stripe company commander each, pressed toward Lam, and recovered all occupied ground.

sentences.zh: 越民苦法虐久，聞馮軍至，皆來迎，爭相犒問，子材招慰安集之，定剿盪北圻策。

translations.literal: The Vietnamese had long suffered French cruelty; hearing that Feng's army had come, they all came to welcome him and vied to offer gifts and inquiries; Zicai comforted and gathered them and fixed a plan to pacify northern Tonkin.
translations.idiomatic: The Vietnamese, long abused by the French, came out to welcome Feng's army with gifts; he reassured them and laid plans to sweep northern Tonkin.

sentences.zh: 越人爭立團，樹馮軍幟，願供糧運作鄉導。

translations.literal: The Vietnamese vied to form militia companies, raised Feng's banners, and offered to supply grain and serve as guides.
translations.idiomatic: They formed militia bands under Feng's banners and offered grain and guides.

sentences.zh: 北寧、河內、海陽、太原競響，子材亦毅然自任。

translations.literal: Bac Ninh, Hanoi, Hai Duong, and Thai Nguyen answered in succession, and Zicai also boldly took the burden on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Bac Ninh, Hanoi, Hai Duong, and Thai Nguyen rose in turn, and Feng boldly accepted the task.

sentences.zh: 於是率全軍攻郎甲，分兵襲北寧，而罷戰詔下，子材憤，請戰，不報，乃挈軍還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the whole army to attack Lang Giá, detached troops to strike Bac Ninh, but the ceasefire edict arrived; Zicai was angry, requested battle, received no reply, and so led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Lang Giá with the main force and sent a column against Bac Ninh; but the ceasefire arrived. Enraged, he asked to fight on, got no answer, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 去之日，越人啼泣遮道，子材亦揮涕不能已。

translations.literal: On the day of departure the Vietnamese wept and blocked the road; Zicai also waved away tears and could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: As he left, Vietnamese wept and blocked the road; Feng too wept and could not compose himself.

sentences.zh: 入關至龍州，軍民拜迎者三十里。

translations.literal: Entering the pass as far as Longzhou, soldiers and civilians came out to welcome him for thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Back inside the pass at Longzhou, troops and people welcomed him for thirty li.

sentences.zh: 命督辦欽、廉防務，會辦廣西軍務，晉太子少保，改三等輕車都尉。

translations.literal: He was ordered to superintend the defenses of Qinzhou and Lianzhou and to assist in Guangxi military affairs; he was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and changed to third-class Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to superintend Qin and Lian defenses and assist Guangxi military affairs, promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and given third-class Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 十三年，討平瓊州黎匪，降敕褒嘉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he campaigned against and pacified the Li bandits of Qiongzhou; an imperial rescript praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he suppressed the Qiongzhou Li bandits and received an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 調雲南提督，稱疾暫留。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Yunnan but pleaded illness and remained temporarily.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yunnan governor, he pleaded illness and stayed on temporarily.

sentences.zh: 二十年，加尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was given the rank of minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he received ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 值中日失和，命募舊部至江南待調發。

translations.literal: When China and Japan fell out, he was ordered to recruit his old troops to the lower Yangtze to await deployment.
translations.idiomatic: When war with Japan broke out, he was told to raise his old units to the lower Yangtze for assignment.

sentences.zh: 和議成，還防。

translations.literal: When peace was made, he returned to his defense post.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，赴本官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he went to his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he took up his regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，入省籌防，會拳亂作，請募勁旅入衛，上嘉其忠勇，止之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he entered the province to plan defenses; when the Boxer rising occurred he asked to recruit crack troops to guard the capital; the throne praised his loyalty and courage but stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he came in to plan defense; when the Boxers rose he asked to bring picked troops to guard the capital—the throne praised his loyalty but forbade it.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，調貴州。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，病免。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was dismissed on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year illness ended his service.

sentences.zh: 明年，廣西土寇蜂起，岑春煊請其出治團防。

translations.literal: The next year bandits rose everywhere in Guangxi; Cen Chunxuan asked him to come out to organize local defense.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Guangxi bandits swarmed; Cen Chunxuan asked him to organize local defense again.

sentences.zh: 方募練成軍，率二子以進，而遘疾困篤。

translations.literal: Just as he had recruited and trained an army and was leading his two sons forward, he was stricken with grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: He had just drilled a force and was marching with his two sons when a severe illness seized him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年八十六，諡勇毅，予建祠。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged eighty-six; posthumous title Yongyi; a temple was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he died, aged eighty-six, posthumous name Yongyi, with permission to build a memorial temple.

sentences.zh: 子材軀幹不逾中人，而硃顏鶴髮，健捷雖少壯弗如。

translations.literal: Zicai's frame did not exceed that of an ordinary man, yet his face was ruddy and his hair white; in vigor and agility even youths could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was no taller than average, yet ruddy-faced and white-haired, and swifter than men half his age.

sentences.zh: 生平不解作欺人語，發餉躬自監視，偶稍短，即罪司軍糈者。

translations.literal: In his life he never knew how to speak deceitfully; when pay was issued he personally supervised it, and if it was even slightly short he punished the commissary officer.
translations.idiomatic: He never lied; he watched pay issues himself and punished the ration officer for the slightest shortfall.

sentences.zh: 治軍四十餘年，寒素如故。

translations.literal: Though he commanded troops for more than forty years, he remained as poor as before.
translations.idiomatic: After forty years of command he lived as plainly as ever.

sentences.zh: 言及國樑，輒涔涔淚下，人皆稱為良將雲。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of Guoliang he would shed tears; all called him a good general.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of Guoliang always brought tears; all agreed he was a true general.

sentences.zh: 王孝祺，本名得勝，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Wang Xiaoqi, original name Desheng, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaoqi, born Desheng, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初入淮軍，以敢戰名。

translations.literal: He first entered the Huai Army and was famed for daring in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Huai Army early and won fame for bold fighting.

sentences.zh: 從李鴻章規三吳，積勳至守備。

translations.literal: He followed Li Hongzhang in recovering the three Wu regions and through merit rose to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Li Hongzhang in recovering the lower Yangtze, he rose by merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 又從張樹聲克常、昭諸城，釋平湖圍，歷遷副將。

translations.literal: He also followed Zhang Shusheng in taking the cities of Chang and Zhao, lifted the siege of Pinghu, and was promoted through several steps to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhang Shusheng he took Chang and Zhao cities, raised the siege of Pinghu, and advanced to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 論克宜、荊、溧、嘉、常功，擢總兵，賜號壯勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: For merit in taking Yi, Jing, Li, Jia, and Chang he was promoted to regional commander and granted the title Zhuangyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing Yi, Jing, Li, Jia, and Chang he became regional commander and received the title Zhuangyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 從援浙，連下湖州、長興。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign to aid Zhejiang and in succession took Huzhou and Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to aid Zhejiang, he took Huzhou and Changxing in turn.

sentences.zh: 是時，樹聲弟樹珊攻湖北德安陣亡，坐失主將，貶秩。

translations.literal: At that time Shusheng's younger brother Shushan died attacking De'an in Hubei; for losing the commanding general he was reduced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shusheng's brother Shushan fell attacking De'an in Hubei; Wang was demoted for the loss of the chief commander.

sentences.zh: 戰敗東捻，復故官。

translations.literal: Defeating the eastern Nian restored his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Beating the eastern Nian restored his rank.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，晉提督，更勇號為博奇。

translations.literal: When the western Nian were pacified he was advanced to military governor and his heroic title was changed to Boqi.
translations.idiomatic: After the western Nian were crushed he became military governor and his heroic title became Boqi.

sentences.zh: 旋赴山西防河，大搜馬賊。

translations.literal: Soon after he went to Shanxi to guard the Yellow River and conducted a major search for mounted bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Shanxi to guard the Yellow River and hunted mounted bandits on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 值晉飢，斥家財以濟，民德之，賊所竄匿，輒先诇以告。

translations.literal: When famine struck Shanxi he spent his family wealth for relief; the people were grateful, and wherever bandits hid they would inform him first.
translations.idiomatic: During Shanxi famine he spent his own wealth on relief; grateful people tipped him off wherever bandits hid.

sentences.zh: 事寧，賜頭品秩。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was granted first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he received the first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，聲督督兩廣，奏自隨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu, when Shusheng became governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi, he memorialized to have Xiaoqi follow him.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year six, when Shusheng became governor-general of the two Guangs, he brought Xiaoqi with him.

sentences.zh: 歷署潮州、碣石總兵。

translations.literal: He successively acted as regional commander of Chaozhou and Jieshi.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as regional commander at Chaozhou and Jieshi in turn.

sentences.zh: 九年，徙右江鎮，主欽、廉防務。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was moved to Youjiang command and took charge of Qin and Lian defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was posted to Youjiang and took Qin-Lian defense.

sentences.zh: 明年，潘鼎新來乞師，領勤軍赴龍州，而鼎新已遁，乃從子材詣鎮南關截潰勇。

translations.literal: The next year Pan Dingxin came begging for troops; he led the Qin Army to Longzhou, but Dingxin had already fled, so he followed Zicai to Zhennan Pass to intercept the routed troops.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Pan Dingxin begged for troops; he led the Qin Army to Longzhou, found Pan had fled, and joined Feng at Zhennan Pass to rally the routed.

sentences.zh: 宵襲文淵，入街心，馬踣，亟易騎，率死士繞山後，攀崖上，破二壘。

translations.literal: At night he raided Van Tien, reached the middle of the street, his horse fell, he quickly changed mounts, led picked men around behind the hills, climbed the cliffs, and broke two stockades.
translations.idiomatic: By night he raided Van Tien to the town center; when his horse fell he remounted, led picked men over the hills, scaled the cliffs, and took two forts.

sentences.zh: 俄而法軍分路入，直攻關前隘，復自後路仰擊，敵稍卻。

translations.literal: Presently the French army entered by separate routes and attacked the pass before the gate head-on; he also struck from the rear up the slope, and the enemy fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The French then came in columns straight at the pass while he hit them from the rear up the slope and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 李秉衡集諸將舉前敵主帥，孝祺曰：「今無論湘、粵、淮軍，宜並受馮公節度。

translations.literal: Li Bingheng gathered the generals to choose a front commander; Xiaoqi said: "Whether Hunan, Guangdong, or Huai troops, all should now accept General Feng's command."
translations.idiomatic: Li Bingheng asked the generals to name a front commander; Xiaoqi said, "Hunan, Guangdong, or Huai—everyone should answer to General Feng."

sentences.zh: 」秉衡稱善。

translations.literal: Bingheng approved.
translations.idiomatic: Bingheng agreed.

sentences.zh: 右路者西嶺也，其部將潘瀛袒臂裸體，衝入敵陣，故傷亡獨多。

translations.literal: The right wing was the western ridge; his subordinate Pan Ying, bare-armed and stripped to the waist, charged into the enemy line, so casualties were especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The right was the western ridge; his officer Pan Ying charged bare-chested into the enemy, so losses there were heaviest.

sentences.zh: 至日暮，孝祺擊敗之，奪三壘而還。

translations.literal: By evening Xiaoqi had defeated them and took three stockades before returning.
translations.idiomatic: By dusk Xiaoqi had beaten them and retook three forts.

sentences.zh: 攻諒城，瀛執幟先登，並力克之，城复。

translations.literal: Attacking Lang Son, Ying seized the banner and climbed first; together they stormed it and the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: At Lang Son, Ying took the colors and scaled the wall first; together they retook the city.

sentences.zh: 取太原，予世職。

translations.literal: He took Thai Nguyen and was granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: He took Thai Nguyen and received a hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，授北海鎮總兵。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed regional commander of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he was made regional commander of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 二十年，賞雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was rewarded with double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he received double peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，謝病歸。

translations.literal: After a year he retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he retired ill.

sentences.zh: 越四年卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: Four years later he died; condolence gifts followed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Four years on he died; mourning honors followed statute.

sentences.zh: 陳嘉，字慶餘，籍廣西荔浦。

translations.literal: Chen Jia, style name Qingyu, registered domicile Lipu in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jia, courtesy name Qingyu, was registered at Lipu in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 從蘇元春徵黔苗，累勳至副將，賜號訥思欽巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He followed Su Yuanchun in campaigning against the Guizhou Miao, accumulated merit to vice commander, and was granted the title Nesiqin Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Su Yuanchun against the Guizhou Miao he rose to vice commander and received the title Nesiqin Batulu.

sentences.zh: 平六硐，擢總兵，調赴湖南守寶慶。

translations.literal: When the six caves were pacified he was promoted to regional commander and transferred to Hunan to defend Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: After the six caves were pacified he became regional commander and was sent to guard Baoqing in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 鼎新撫廣東，嘉引兵從。

translations.literal: When Dingxin became governor of Guangdong, Jia led his troops to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When Pan Dingxin governed Guangdong, Chen brought his troops to follow.

sentences.zh: 抵思恩，值土寇嘯亂，計擒其魁莫思弼，誅之。

translations.literal: Reaching Si'en, he encountered local bandits in uproar; he planned and captured their leader Mo Sibbi and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Si'en amid bandit unrest, he seized their chief Mo Sibbi and executed him.

sentences.zh: 法越之役，率鎮南軍出關扼谷松。

translations.literal: In the Franco-Vietnamese war he led the Zhennan army beyond the pass to hold Gusong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sino-French War he led the Zhennan army out to block Gusong.

sentences.zh: 敵至，砲甚猛，退頓堅老，已而戰船頭、陸岸，皆捷。

translations.literal: When the enemy came their cannon fire was very fierce; he withdrew and encamped at Jianlao, but soon won victories both at Zhan Chuan Tou and on the land bank.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came with heavy fire; he fell back to Jianlao, then won at ship-head and on the shore.

sentences.zh: 法軍據紙作社，師設伏誘之，嘉出挑戰，敵悉眾迎拒，戰方酣，元春隱兵起，斬法將四人、兵二百八十餘。

translations.literal: The French held Zhi Zuo She; the army set an ambush to lure them—Jia came out to challenge, the enemy met him with their full strength, and as battle grew hot Yuanchun's hidden troops rose and killed four French officers and more than 280 soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At Paper-Making Society the French were lured into an ambush: Chen challenged, they met with full force, and as fighting peaked Su's hidden troops cut down four French officers and over 280 men.

sentences.zh: 捷入，賞黃馬褂，授貴州安義鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket and appointed regional commander of Anyi in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Victory brought a yellow riding jacket and appointment as Anyi regional commander in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，法軍大舉寇​​堅老，鏖戰數晝夜，被重創僕地，左右掖之去，既覺，麾刀叱退，仍奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: Before long the French attacked Jianlao in force; after several days and nights of fierce fighting he was struck down with grave wounds; his attendants helped him away, but when he came to he waved his sword and drove them back and still fought on to defeat the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The French then stormed Jianlao; after days of battle he fell badly wounded, was carried off, woke, drove his men back with his sword, and still beat the enemy.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，法軍薄長牆。

translations.literal: After a year the French pressed the long wall.
translations.idiomatic: A year on the French pressed the long wall.

sentences.zh: 左路即東嶺，嘉爭其三壘，宗漢繼之，七上七下，嘉被創者四，氣不少沮。

translations.literal: The left wing was the eastern ridge; Jia contested its three stockades and Zonghan followed; seven times up and seven down—Jia was wounded four times yet his spirit did not flag.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern ridge Jia fought seven assaults for three forts, Jiang followed, and Chen took four wounds without faltering.

sentences.zh: 孝祺自西來援，合擊之，遂奪還。

translations.literal: Xiaoqi came to aid from the west; together they struck and recovered them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang came from the west; together they retook the forts.

sentences.zh: 以次復文淵、諒山，進規谷松，力疾赴前敵，詔嘉之，賜頭品秩，予世職。

translations.literal: In succession they recovered Van Tien and Lang Son and advanced on Gusong; though gravely ill he hurried to the front; the court praised him, granted the first-rank cap button, and gave a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: They retook Van Tien and Lang Son and moved on Gusong; Chen dragged himself to the front, won praise, the first-rank button, and a hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 創發，卒於軍，年未五十，諡勇烈。

translations.literal: His wounds reopened and he died in camp, not yet fifty; posthumous title Yonglie.
translations.idiomatic: His wounds reopened; he died in camp before fifty, posthumous name Yonglie.

sentences.zh: 蔣宗漢，籍雲南鶴麗。

translations.literal: Jiang Zonghan was registered in Heli, Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zonghan was registered at Heli in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 同治初，回寇入境，方居憂，其酋馬金寶逼令受先鋒印，佯以終制辭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign Hui rebels entered the border; he was in mourning when their chief Ma Jinbao forced him to accept the vanguard seal, and he pretended to decline on grounds of observing mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, while in mourning, Hui chief Ma Jinbao forced a vanguard seal on him; he feigned refusal on mourning grounds.

sentences.zh: 潛歸里，至江乾，無舟可濟，追騎將及，仰天祝曰：「苟得留身報國，當建此橋！

translations.literal: He secretly returned home; reaching the riverbank there was no boat to cross and pursuing horsemen were about to catch up; he looked to heaven and prayed: "If I may be spared to serve the state, I will build this bridge!"
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing home he reached the river with no boat and pursuers near; he prayed, "If I live to serve the state, I will build this bridge!"

sentences.zh: 」果得浮槎以免。

translations.literal: He indeed found a raft and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: A raft appeared and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 既貴，成金龍橋，亙數百丈，行旅至今賴之。

translations.literal: When he had risen high he built the Jinlong Bridge, spanning several hundred zhang; travelers rely on it to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Once eminent he built Jinlong Bridge, hundreds of zhang long, still used by travelers.

sentences.zh: 初隸楊玉科麾下，每戰輒為先鋒。

translations.literal: At first he served under Yang Yuke and in every battle was always in the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Yang Yuke and always led the van.

sentences.zh: 從攻豬供箐，其下有吳家屯，為寇儲糧地，備奧阻。

translations.literal: In attacking Zhugongqing, below it was Wujiatun, the rebels' grain depot, strongly defended in difficult terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Below Zhugongqing lay Wujiatun, the rebels' grain depot, strongly held.

sentences.zh: 宗漢間道得大溜口，率死士百，縋幽鑿險，忍飢抵壁下，置藥桶，設伏線，潛出約師，火發，大敗之，繇是知名。

translations.literal: Zonghan found a path by a side route to the great ravine mouth, led a hundred picked men, lowered themselves down cliffs and cut through dangers, endured hunger to reach the wall base, placed powder barrels, set trip lines, stole out to coordinate with the main force—when fire broke out the enemy was badly defeated, and from this he became famous.
translations.idiomatic: He found a ravine path, led a hundred men down cliffs, laid powder and fuse lines, coordinated with the main force, and won a crushing victory that made his name.

sentences.zh: 又從玉科迭下各郡邑，積勳至副將，賜號著勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He also followed Yuke in successively taking the prefectures and counties, rose through merit to vice commander, and was granted the title Zhuoyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuke he took city after city, rose to vice commander, and received Zhuoyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 戰小圍埂，勒馬挺矛，當者輒靡。

translations.literal: At the battle of Xiaoweigeng he reined his horse and levelled his spear; whoever faced him fell.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaoweigeng he charged with levelled spear and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 岑毓英見而歎曰：「真虎將也！

translations.literal: Cen Yuying saw it and sighed: "A true tiger general!"
translations.idiomatic: Cen Yuying watched and exclaimed, "A true tiger general!"

sentences.zh: 」大理平，擢提督，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: When Dali was pacified he was promoted to military governor and rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: After Dali fell he became military governor and received a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 攻錫臘、順寧，皆先據要險，設伏敗敵。

translations.literal: In attacking Xila and Shunning he always first seized critical ground and set ambushes to defeat the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At Xila and Shunning he seized key ground and ambushed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 人皆謂其善謀雲。

translations.literal: All said he was skilled in strategy.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed he was a master of stratagem.

sentences.zh: 事寧，更勇號圖桑阿。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled his heroic title was changed to Tusang'a.
translations.idiomatic: After peace his heroic title became Tusang'a.

sentences.zh: 克雲州，署騰越鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He captured Yunzhou and acted as regional commander of Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: He took Yunzhou and acted as Tengyue regional commander.

sentences.zh: 攻克烏索，授順雲協副將。

translations.literal: He captured Wusuo and was appointed assistant regional commander of Shunyun.
translations.idiomatic: He took Wusuo and became Shunyun assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 光緒改元，英繙譯官馬嘉理入滇邊，抵戶宋河遇害，坐疏防，鐫秩付鞫。

translations.literal: When the Guangxu reign began, the British interpreter Margary entered the Yunnan border and was killed at the Husong River; for lax defense he was reduced in rank and handed over for trial.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangxu's start British interpreter Margary was killed on the Yunnan border; Jiang was demoted and tried for lax defense.

sentences.zh: 明年，复騰越，起副將。

translations.literal: The next year Tengyue was recovered and he was reinstated as vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, with Tengyue recovered, he was restored as vice commander.

sentences.zh: 五年，靖遠平，復故官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Jingyuan was pacified and he recovered his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, after Jingyuan was pacified, he regained his rank.

sentences.zh: 法越之役，率廣武軍出關，功與嘉埒。

translations.literal: In the Franco-Vietnamese war he led the Guangwu army beyond the pass; his merit matched Jia's.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sino-French War he led the Guangwu army out; his deeds matched Chen Jia's.

sentences.zh: 和議成，賜頭品秩，除貴州遵義鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When peace was made he was granted the first-rank cap button and appointed regional commander of Zunyi in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he received the first-rank button and became Zunyi regional commander in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年，賞雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was rewarded with double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he received double peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，署提督，調雲南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he acted as military governor and was transferred to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he acted as governor and moved to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 越二年，還貴州，予實授。

translations.literal: Two years later he returned to Guizhou and received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on he returned to Guizhou with full appointment.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，予建祠。

translations.literal: The next year he died; permission to build a temple was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he died; a memorial temple was authorized.

sentences.zh: 蘇元春，字子熙，廣西永安人。

translations.literal: Su Yuanchun, style name Zixi, was a native of Yong'an in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yuanchun, courtesy name Zixi, came from Yong'an in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 父德保，以廩生治鄉團，禦寇被害，州人建祠祀之。

translations.literal: His father Debao, a licentiate who organized local militia, was killed resisting bandits; the prefecture built a temple to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Debao, a licentiate who led local militia, died fighting bandits; the district built him a temple.

sentences.zh: 元春誓復仇，從湘軍。

translations.literal: Yuanchun swore revenge and joined the Hunan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchun vowed revenge and entered the Hunan Army.

sentences.zh: 同治初，隨席寶田援贛、皖、粵，累功至參將，假歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign he followed Xi Baotian to aid Jiangxi, Anhui, and Guangdong, accumulated merit to regimental commander, and returned on leave.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi he campaigned in Jiangxi, Anhui, and Guangdong under Xi Baotian, rose to regimental commander, and went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 六年，領中軍徵黔苗，破荊竹園，賜號健勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he led the central army against the Guizhou Miao, broke Jingzhuyuan, and was granted the title Jianyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he led the center column against Guizhou Miao, took Jingzhuyuan, and received Jianyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 連克要隘，更號銳勇。

translations.literal: He captured critical passes in succession and his title was changed to Ruiyong.
translations.idiomatic: He took pass after pass and his title became Ruiyong.

sentences.zh: 八年，統右路軍，值思州苗犯鎮遠，复擊卻之，進復清江，擢總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he commanded the right-route army; when Sinan Miao attacked Zhenyuan he drove them back and recovered Qingjiang, and was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he commanded the right wing, repelled Sinan Miao at Zhenyuan, recovered Qingjiang, and became regional commander.

sentences.zh: 黃飄之役，黃潤昌戰死，元春馳救，亦敗退，幹吏議。

translations.literal: In the Huangpiao campaign Huang Runchang died in battle; Yuanchun rushed to rescue but also retreated in defeat, and cadre officials criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangpiao Huang Runchang fell; Su rushed to help but was beaten back and faced censure.

sentences.zh: 克施秉，復故官。

translations.literal: He captured Shibing and recovered his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He took Shibing and regained his rank.

sentences.zh: 九年，攻施洞，拔九股河，又改法什尚阿勇號。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he attacked Shidong, took Jiugu River, and again changed his heroic title to Fashishang'a.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he attacked Shidong, took Jiugu River, and received the title Fashishang'a.

sentences.zh: 薄台拱，苗遁走，晉提督。

translations.literal: Pressing Taigong, the Miao fled; he was advanced to military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing Taigong he drove the Miao off and became military governor.

sentences.zh: 明年，复丹江、凱里，軍威益振，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: The next year he recovered Danjiang and Kaili; military prestige grew still greater and he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he retook Danjiang and Kaili, his fame grew, and he received a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 以次下黃飄、白堡，驛道始通。

translations.literal: In succession he took Huangpiao and Baibao, and the courier road was opened at last.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Huangpiao and Baibao and reopened the courier route.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，循清水而南，所至輒靡，惟烏鴉坡猶負固。

translations.literal: After a year he marched south along the Qingshui River; wherever he went the enemy yielded, only Wuya Po still held out stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he marched south along the Qingshui; all yielded except Wuya Po.

sentences.zh: 復自東南破張秀眉砦。

translations.literal: He again broke Zhang Xiumei's stockade from the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: From the southeast he stormed Zhang Xiumei's fort.

sentences.zh: 殘苗將北走，黔軍遏之河干。

translations.literal: The remnant Miao were about to flee north; Guizhou troops blocked them at the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant Miao fled north but Guizhou troops barred the river.

sentences.zh: 元春麾軍馳之，截寇為二，斬數千級，降三萬餘人，苗砦悉平。

translations.literal: Yuanchun galloped his army thither, cut the bandits in two, killed several thousand, accepted the surrender of more than thirty thousand, and all Miao stockades were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Su raced up, split the enemy, killed thousands, accepted thirty thousand surrenders, and pacified every Miao fort.

sentences.zh: 元春留頓其地，撫降眾。

translations.literal: Yuanchun remained stationed there to pacify the surrendered masses.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed to settle the surrendered.

sentences.zh: 論功，予雲騎尉。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted Cloud Cavalry Captain.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received Cloud Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 全黔底定，賜頭品秩。

translations.literal: When all Guizhou was settled he was granted the first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhou was fully pacified he received the first-rank button.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，平六硐及江華瑤，被賞賚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he pacified the six caves and the Jianghua Yao and received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu he pacified the six caves and Jianghua Yao and was rewarded.

sentences.zh: 十年，和議中變，法人大舉攻桂軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the peace agreement broke down and the French attacked the Guangxi army in force.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year peace collapsed and the French struck the Guangxi army hard.

sentences.zh: 潘鼎新薦其才，詔署提督。

translations.literal: Pan Dingxin recommended his talent and the court ordered him to act as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Dingxin praised him and the court named him acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 遂率毅新軍駐谷松，取陸岸，鏖戰五晝夜。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the Yixin army to garrison Gusong, took the land bank, and fought fiercely for five days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: He led the Yixin army to Gusong, took the shore, and fought five days and nights.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其勇，命佐鼎新軍，再予騎都尉。

translations.literal: The throne praised his courage, ordered him to assist Dingxin's army, and again granted Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised his valor, attached him to Pan's command, and again granted Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 規紙作社，敵緣江築壘，夜將半，師設伏誘之，其左樹木幽深，元春隱兵其中，敵至，於是夾擊，大破虜。

translations.literal: Planning against Zhi Zuo She, the enemy built stockades along the river; near midnight the army set an ambush to lure them—the left had deep woods where Yuanchun hid troops; when the enemy came they were struck from both sides and badly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Paper-Making Society the French built river forts; near midnight an ambush lured them—Su hid in the woods left of the line and crushed them in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 既而法人犯谷松，師連戰失利。

translations.literal: Presently the French attacked Gusong and the army suffered defeat in successive battles.
translations.idiomatic: Then the French hit Gusong and the army lost battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 敵毀鎮南關，元春出隴窯御之，不克，退幕府。

translations.literal: The enemy destroyed Zhennan Pass; Yuanchun went out to Longyao to resist but could not prevail and withdrew to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: They burned Zhennan Pass; Su met them at Longyao, failed, and fell back to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 當是時，自南寧至桂林，居民大震。

translations.literal: At that time from Nanning to Guilin the inhabitants were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: From Nanning to Guilin the people were terrified.

sentences.zh: 鼎新罷免，遂命主廣西軍事。

translations.literal: Dingxin was dismissed and Yuanchun was then put in chief command of Guangxi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pan was removed and Su took chief command in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，法人寇西路，元春趨艽封截之，乃引去。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the French raided the western route; Yuanchun hurried to Qiongfeng to intercept them and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the French raided the west; Su rushed to Qiongfeng and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俄攻關前隘，失三壘，元春亟馳救。

translations.literal: Soon they attacked the pass before the gate and took three stockades; Yuanchun rushed to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: They then took three forts at the pass; Su raced to save it.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，助子材扼中路，大捷，語具子材傳。

translations.literal: At dawn he assisted Zicai in holding the center route and won a great victory—the account is given in Zicai's biography.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he held the center with Feng and won greatly—as told in Feng's biography.

sentences.zh: 長驅文淵，元春踵至，诇知敵據驅驢墟，乘其未整列逐之，敵奪門走，進扼觀音橋，而停戰詔下，諸軍分頓關內，元春駐憑祥，居中調度。

translations.literal: Driving on to Van Tien, Yuanchun followed close; learning the enemy held Qulüxu he struck before they could form ranks and drove them out the gate, advanced to hold Guanyin Bridge, but the ceasefire edict came down; the armies stationed inside the pass and Yuanchun garrisoned Pingxiang, directing affairs from the center.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed to Van Tien, caught the French at Qulüxu before they formed, drove them out, held Guanyin Bridge—then ceasefire came; armies withdrew and Su directed from Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 和議成，授提督，晉三等輕車都尉，又改額爾德蒙額勇號。

translations.literal: When peace was made he was appointed military governor, advanced to third-class Commandant of Light Chariots, and his heroic title was again changed to E'erdemeng'e Yong.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he became governor, third-class Commandant of Light Chariots, with title E'erdemeng'e Yong.

sentences.zh: 還龍州，其南曰連城，號天險，建行台其上，暇輒取健兒練校之，授以兵法。

translations.literal: Returning to Longzhou, to its south was Liancheng, called impregnable by nature; he built a field headquarters on it and in leisure would take stalwart men to drill and teach them tactics.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Longzhou he built headquarters on natural fortress Liancheng and drilled picked men in tactics.

sentences.zh: 西四十里即關，崇山相崟，一道中達。

translations.literal: Forty li west was the pass, with lofty mountains facing each other and a single road between.
translations.idiomatic: Forty li west lay the pass, mountains towering on either side with one road through.

sentences.zh: 元春相形勝，築砲台百三十所，囑統將馬盛治鎮之。

translations.literal: Yuanchun surveyed the terrain and built one hundred thirty gun platforms, entrusting their command to Ma Shengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He built 130 gun platforms and left Ma Shengzhi to command them.

sentences.zh: 鑿險徑，闢市場，民、僮懽忭。

translations.literal: He cut paths through the cliffs and opened markets; Han and Zhuang rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: He cut cliff paths and opened markets; Han and Zhuang were delighted.

sentences.zh: 復自關外達龍州，創建鐵路百餘裡，增兵勇，設製造局，屹然為西南重鎮。

translations.literal: He also extended from beyond the pass to Longzhou, created more than a hundred li of road, increased troops, and established an arsenal—standing firm as the great stronghold of the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: He linked the pass to Longzhou with over a hundred li of road, added troops and an arsenal, and made a southwest stronghold.

sentences.zh: 加太子少保，晉二等輕車都尉。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and second-class Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and second-class Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，入覲，命赴廣州灣劃界。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he had an audience and was ordered to Guangzhou Bay to delimit the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was summoned to court and sent to delimit Guangzhou Bay.

sentences.zh: 前後鎮邊凡十九年，閱時久，師律漸弛，兵與盜合而為一，蔓滋廣。

translations.literal: In all he guarded the frontier for nineteen years; as time passed discipline gradually slackened and soldiers merged with bandits, which spread ever wider.
translations.idiomatic: He guarded the border nineteen years; discipline slackened until troops and bandits became one scourge.

sentences.zh: 朝命岑春煊督兩粵治之，御史周樹模劾元春演餉縱寇，敕春煊按覆。

translations.literal: The court ordered Cen Chunxuan to govern the two Guangs and settle it; censor Zhou Shumo memorialized that Yuanchun inflated pay and indulged bandits; the throne ordered Chunxuan to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Chunxuan was sent to govern the two Guangs; censor Zhou Shumo accused Su of padding pay and tolerating bandits; the throne ordered inquiry.

sentences.zh: 春煊謂不斬元春無以嚴戎備，詔奪職逮訊。

translations.literal: Chunxuan said that without executing Yuanchun military discipline could not be tightened, and an edict stripped his office and ordered arrest and interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Cen said Su must die to restore discipline; an edict stripped him and ordered arrest.

sentences.zh: 初，湘軍舊制，軍餉月資衣食外，餘存主將所備緩急，歲餘乃給之，名曰「存餉」。

translations.literal: Formerly under Hunan Army practice, beyond monthly pay for food and clothing the remainder was kept by the commanding general for emergencies and only issued at year's end—it was called "stored pay."
translations.idiomatic: Under Hunan Army custom, after monthly rations the surplus stayed with the commander for emergencies and was paid at year-end as "stored pay."

sentences.zh: 元春蒞邊，凡所設施，不足，移十二萬濟之。

translations.literal: When Yuanchun came to the frontier all his projects fell short; he drew on 120,000 taels to cover them.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier his projects ran short and he drew 120,000 taels from stored pay.

sentences.zh: 刑部擬以斬監候，獄急，元春請以應領公款十六萬備抵償。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishments proposed decapitation after the autumn assizes; the case was urgent; Yuanchun asked to use 160,000 taels of pay due him to make restitution.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry proposed execution after autumn assizes; Su offered 160,000 taels of owed pay to make good the loss.

sentences.zh: 於是部再疏其狀，謂其父死難，例得減，詔戍新疆。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ministry again memorialized the facts, saying that because his father had died in service he was entitled to reduction by statute, and an edict sentenced him to service in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry cited his father's death in service and the throne commuted him to exile in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 元春軀幹雄碩，不治生產，然輕財好士，能得人死力。

translations.literal: Yuanchun had a large, imposing frame and did not attend to production, yet he was free with wealth and fond of nurturing men, and could win men's death-defying loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Su was big-framed and careless of wealth, yet generous to warriors and able to command absolute loyalty.

sentences.zh: 嘗與法人接，獨持大體。

translations.literal: He had dealings with the French and alone upheld the larger proprieties.
translations.idiomatic: In dealing with the French he alone upheld proper statecraft.

sentences.zh: 金龍峒者，安平土州地，為中、越要隘，法將據之，與爭不決。

translations.literal: Jinlongdong was territory of Anping native prefecture, a critical pass between China and Vietnam; a French officer held it and contention was unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Jinlongdong in Anping was a Sino-Vietnamese choke point held by the French in unresolved dispute.

sentences.zh: 而游勇萬人恆出沒為法患，法莫能製。

translations.literal: Yet ten thousand irregulars constantly came and went to plague the French, whom they could not control.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand irregulars harried the French beyond their control.

sentences.zh: 其總督入關來求助，元春悉召至資遣之，金龍七隘卒歸隸。

translations.literal: Their governor-general entered the pass to ask help; Yuanchun summoned them all and provided funds to send them away, and the seven passes of Jinlong at last returned to jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The French governor came for help; Su gathered the irregulars, paid them off, and recovered the seven Jinlong passes.

sentences.zh: 法商李約德為寇所掠，總署慮啟釁，以屬元春。

translations.literal: The French merchant Li Yuede was plundered by bandits; the Zongli Yamen feared provocation and referred the matter to Yuanchun.
translations.idiomatic: French merchant Li Yuede was robbed; the Foreign Office feared trouble and referred it to Su.

sentences.zh: 元春簡騶從詣山下，寇聞，送之出。

translations.literal: Yuanchun took only a small escort to the foot of the hills; when the bandits heard, they sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: Su went to the hills with a small escort; the bandits heard and released the captive.

sentences.zh: 時元春已積逋二十萬，或勸其請諸朝，元春歎曰：「吾任邊事，致外人蹈絕險，尚敢欺朝廷要重利乎？

translations.literal: By then Yuanchun already owed 200,000 taels; some urged him to petition the court, but Yuanchun sighed: "I held frontier affairs and let foreigners tread extreme danger—how dare I deceive the court to demand heavy profit?"
translations.idiomatic: He owed 200,000 taels; some urged a court petition, but he said, "I let foreigners risk their lives on my border—how dare I cheat the throne for profit?"

sentences.zh: 」卒不可。

translations.literal: In the end he would not.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 法感其義，贈寶星。

translations.literal: The French were moved by his righteousness and presented him a decoration.
translations.idiomatic: The French honored his integrity with a decoration.

sentences.zh: 既入獄，年已六十矣，無子，幕士董左右之。

translations.literal: After he entered prison he was already sixty, without sons; a staff officer named Dong attended him constantly.
translations.idiomatic: In prison at sixty, childless, staff officer Dong stayed by him.

sentences.zh: 法總統聞其狀，急電公使端貴等謀緩頰。

translations.literal: The French president heard of his situation and urgently telegraphed the minister Duan Gui and others to seek clemency.
translations.idiomatic: The French president telegraphed Minister Duan Gui to plead for mercy.

sentences.zh: 喜，具以告，元春曰：「法，吾仇也。

translations.literal: Dong was pleased and told him fully; Yuanchun said: "The French are my enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Dong rejoiced and told him; Su said, "The French are my enemies.

sentences.zh: 死則死耳，藉仇以乞生，是重辱也！

translations.literal: Die and that is all—begging life through an enemy is redoubled disgrace!"
translations.idiomatic: Death is death—begging life through an enemy doubles the shame!"

sentences.zh: 君為我謝之。

translations.literal: Please thank them for me.
translations.idiomatic: Please thank them for me."

sentences.zh: 」居戍四年，御史李灼華疏其冤，事下張人駿，廉得實，請釋歸，而已卒於迪化。

translations.literal: "He lived in exile four years; censor Li Zhuohua memorialized his injustice; the case went to Zhang Renjun, who investigated and found the facts and requested release—but he had already died at Dihua.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in exile, censor Li Zhuohua pleaded his innocence; Zhang Renjun verified the facts and sought release—but he had already died at Dihua.

sentences.zh: 貧無斂，新疆布政使王樹棻為治其喪。

translations.literal: He was too poor for burial; Wang Shufen, financial commissioner of Xinjiang, arranged his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor for burial, Xinjiang treasurer Wang Shufen arranged his funeral.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，复官，子承賜，戍所生。

translations.literal: When the Xuantong reign began his office was restored; his son Chengcisi was ennobled and born in exile.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuantong his rank was restored; son Chengcisi was ennobled, born in exile.

sentences.zh: 馬盛治，字仲平，籍廣西永安。

translations.literal: Ma Shengzhi, style name Zhongping, was registered in Yong'an, Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shengzhi, courtesy name Zhongping, was registered at Yong'an in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 以孝著。

translations.literal: He was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 初隨席寶田徵黔苗，積功至游擊，賜號壯勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: At first he followed Xi Baotian against the Guizhou Miao, accumulated merit to mobile corps commander, and was granted the title Zhuangyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He first campaigned under Xi Baotian against Guizhou Miao, rose to mobile corps commander, and received Zhuangyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 苗疆平，更勇號哈豐阿，遷副將。

translations.literal: When the Miao frontier was pacified his heroic title was changed to Hafeng'a and he was transferred to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the Miao frontier was pacified his title became Hafeng'a and he became vice commander.

sentences.zh: 從克六硐，擢總兵。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing the six caves and was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take the six caves and was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 越事急，遂率師出關。

translations.literal: When the Vietnamese affair grew urgent he led his army beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the Vietnamese crisis sharpened he marched out beyond the pass.

sentences.zh: 時宣光、太原、牧馬潰勇索餉譁變，盛治輕騎往撫，汰弱留強，軍紀以肅。

translations.literal: At that time routed troops at Xuanguang, Thai Nguyen, and Muma were mutinying for pay; Shengzhi went with a light escort to pacify them, weeded out the weak and kept the strong, and army discipline was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Routed troops at Xuanguang, Thai Nguyen, and Muma mutinied for pay; Ma went lightly to pacify them, kept the strong, and restored discipline.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，法人悉銳至，腹背受敵。

translations.literal: After a year the French came with their full elite strength and he was attacked front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: A year on the French came in full strength and he was caught front and rear.

sentences.zh: 盛治具餱糧，間道繞敵前，與元春諸軍夾擊之，遂復南關。

translations.literal: Shengzhi prepared rations and by a side path circled before the enemy, joined Yuanchun's armies in a pincer, and recovered the southern pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ma supplied rations, outflanked the enemy, pincered with Su's forces, and retook the southern pass.

sentences.zh: 克文淵、諒山、長慶，頻有功，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He captured Van Tien, Lang Son, and Changqing, won repeated merit, and was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He took Van Tien, Lang Son, and Changqing, won repeated honors, and received a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 光緒十二年，除柳慶鎮總兵，仍統邊軍佐元春，築砲台，設廛市，賞雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Guangxu he was appointed regional commander of Liuqing and still commanded frontier troops assisting Yuanchun, built gun platforms, opened markets, and was rewarded with double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year twelve he became Liuqing regional commander, still aided Su on the frontier, built forts and markets, and received double peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，會辦中越界務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he assisted in Sino-Vietnamese boundary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he assisted in the Sino-Vietnamese boundary.

sentences.zh: 連破西林、鬱林諸匪，晉提督。

translations.literal: He successively defeated bandits in Xilin and Yulin and was advanced to military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Xilin and Yulin bandits in turn and became military governor.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，移署左江鎮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to act as commander of Zuojiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he acted as Zuojiang commander.

sentences.zh: 南寧各屬故盜藪，至即麾軍搜剿，寇聞風遁。

translations.literal: The districts around Nanning had long been bandit haunts; on arrival he sent troops to search and suppress, and bandits fled at the news.
translations.idiomatic: Nanning districts were longtime bandit nests; he swept them and bandits fled at his name.

sentences.zh: 遂檄所屬練團築卡，堅壁清野，寇大困。

translations.literal: He then ordered subordinates to drill militia and build checkpoints, cleared the fields and villages, and the bandits were greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered militia checkpoints and cleared the countryside, strangling the bandits.

sentences.zh: 其酋黃和順等猶負嵎，官軍攻隴賴，遇伏，槍彈雨坌，盛治被重創，眾掖之出，旋卒。

translations.literal: Their chiefs Huang Heshun and others still held out; government troops attacked Longlai, met an ambush, bullets fell like rain, Shengzhi was gravely wounded, the men helped him out, and soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Huang Heshun still held out; at Longlai an ambush gravely wounded Ma; his men carried him out and he soon died.

sentences.zh: 盛治居邊十七年，元春倚如左右手。

translations.literal: Shengzhi had been on the frontier seventeen years; Yuanchun relied on him like right hand and left.
translations.idiomatic: Ma served the frontier seventeen years; Su relied on him as on his own hands.

sentences.zh: 元春尚寬，而盛治濟以嚴，邊境賴以寧謐。

translations.literal: Yuanchun was inclined to leniency while Shengzhi supplemented with severity, and the border depended on this for tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: Su was lenient; Ma added severity, and the border stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八，諡武烈，予思恩、南寧建祠。

translations.literal: When he died, aged fifty-eight, posthumous title Wulie; temples were granted at Si'en and Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight, posthumous name Wulie, with temples at Si'en and Nanning.

sentences.zh: 王德榜，字朗青，湖南江華人。

translations.literal: Wang Debang, style name Langqing, was a native of Jianghua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Debang, courtesy name Langqing, came from Jianghua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，粵寇擾境，與兄吉昌毀家起鄉兵，戰數利。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign Cantonese rebels disturbed the border; with his elder brother Jichang he ruined his family to raise local troops and won several victories.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng, Cantonese rebels raided the border; he and his brother Jichang spent their fortune raising militia and won repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 五年，援江西，攻奉新，吉昌戰死，德榜領其眾，誓復仇。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he aided Jiangxi and attacked Fengxin; Jichang died in battle and Debang took command of his troops, swearing revenge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he aided Jiangxi at Fengxin; Jichang fell and Debang took his men, vowing revenge.

sentences.zh: 七年，論克瑞州功，敘經歷、州同。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, for merit in taking Ruizhou, he was given the ranks of experiences clerk and prefectural sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, for taking Ruizhou, he received clerk and sub-prefect ranks.

sentences.zh: 明年，從將軍福興援浙，复衢、處各城，擢知州。

translations.literal: The next year he followed General Fuxing to aid Zhejiang, recovered Qu and Chu cities, and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Next year under General Fuxing he aided Zhejiang, retook Qu and Chu, and became prefect.

sentences.zh: 又明年，從援安徽，克婺源，遷直隸州知州，援例加道員。

translations.literal: The year after he followed the campaign to aid Anhui, captured Wuyuan, was transferred to prefect of Zhili prefecture, and by precedent was given circuit intendant rank.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he aided Anhui, took Wuyuan, became Zhili prefect, and received intendant rank by precedent.

sentences.zh: 其夏，殲賊浮梁景德鎮。

translations.literal: That summer he destroyed the bandits at Fuliang and Jingdezhen.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he destroyed bandits at Fuliang and Jingdezhen.

sentences.zh: 十年，平廣信，寇遁入浙。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he pacified Guangxin and the bandits fled into Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he pacified Guangxin and drove bandits into Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 徙防玉山，歸左宗棠節度。

translations.literal: He moved to defend Yushan and returned to Zuo Zongtang's command.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Yushan under Zuo Zongtang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，李世賢、李秀成先後來犯，並擊卻之，賜號銳勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Li Shixian and Li Xiucheng came to attack in succession; he beat them back both times and was granted the title Ruiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Li Shixian and Li Xiucheng attacked in turn; he repulsed both and received Ruiyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 同治改元，所部譁變，又不禀宗棠命，私越境駐廣豐，褫職留軍。

translations.literal: When the Tongzhi reign began his troops mutinied, and again without reporting to Zongtang he privately crossed the border to garrison Guangfeng; his office was stripped but he remained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongzhi his troops mutinied; he crossed into Guangfeng without orders, was stripped of office but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 尋還浙。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 世賢犯遂安，出常山、華埠截之。

translations.literal: Shixian attacked Suian; he went out by Changshan and Huabu to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: When Shixian attacked Suian he intercepted by Changshan and Huabu.

sentences.zh: 會宗棠耀兵龍遊，令扼全旺。

translations.literal: When Zongtang displayed his army at Longyou he ordered Debang to hold Quanwang.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang massed at Longyou and ordered Debang to hold Quanwang.

sentences.zh: 世賢遣驍賊分道馳救，德榜自右路夾擊，皆愕走。

translations.literal: Shixian sent fierce bandits by separate routes to the rescue; Debang struck from the right wing in a pincer and they fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian sent crack troops to relieve the city; Debang hit the right wing and routed them.

sentences.zh: 城寇猶未下，逾歲，偪城南，築三壘，寇夜遁，复官。

translations.literal: The city bandits were not yet down; after a year he pressed the south of the city and built three stockades; the bandits fled by night and his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The city still held; a year on he pressed the south, built three forts, the enemy fled by night, and his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 移師浮梁，連下崇光、陽溪諸渡。

translations.literal: He moved his army to Fuliang and in succession took the crossings at Chongguang, Yangxi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Fuliang and took Chongguang, Yangxi, and other crossings.

sentences.zh: 三年，釋廣信圍。

translations.literal: In the third year he lifted the siege of Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he raised the siege of Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 其秋，復東鄉，長驅江山、玉山、廣豐、鉛山，所至皆下，擢按察使。

translations.literal: That autumn he recovered Dongxiang and drove through Jiangshan, Yushan, Guangfeng, and Qianshan; wherever he went all submitted, and he was promoted to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he recovered Dongxiang and swept Jiangshan, Yushan, Guangfeng, and Qianshan, becoming surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時，世賢合汪海洋出入江、廣邊，連陷龍巖、南靖、漳州。

translations.literal: At that time Shixian joined Wang Haiyang in raiding the Jiangxi-Guangdong border and in succession took Longyan, Nanjing, and Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shixian and Wang Haiyang raided the Jiang-Guang border and took Longyan, Nanjing, and Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 德榜將二千五百人馳援，合劉典軍為西路軍，攻莒溪，克之。

translations.literal: Debang led twenty-five hundred men in urgent relief, joined Liu Dian's army as the western-route force, attacked Juxi, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Debang rushed two thousand five hundred men to join Liu Dian's western column, took Juxi.

sentences.zh: 四年春，授福建按察使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he was appointed surveillance commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fourth year he became Fujian surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 復古田，攻南陽，師少卻。

translations.literal: He recovered Gutian and attacked Nanyang; the army was few and fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Gutian and attacked Nanyang but fell back when outnumbered.

sentences.zh: 俄而海洋率黃、白號悍黨可二萬列田壟，典先入，德榜為承，奮擊之，寇返西岸。

translations.literal: Presently Haiyang led about twenty thousand fierce Yellow- and White-Banner partisans in battle lines on the field ridges; Dian entered first, Debang supported, and they struck hard—the bandits retreated to the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyang brought twenty thousand Yellow- and White-Banner diehards; Liu Dian led in, Debang supported, and drove them to the west bank.

sentences.zh: 德榜追至下車，海洋下馬痛哭，其黨挾之走。

translations.literal: Debang pursued to Xiache; Haiyang dismounted and wept bitterly, and his followers seized him and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Debang pursued to Xiache; Haiyang wept, dismounted, and his men dragged him away.

sentences.zh: 黃、白號衣者，海洋所蓄死士，號無敵，至是喪失過半矣。

translations.literal: The Yellow- and White-Banner men were Haiyang's household troops, called invincible; more than half were lost on this day.
translations.idiomatic: His Yellow- and White-Banner household troops, called invincible, lost more than half that day.

sentences.zh: 四月，邀擊世賢於安溪，進攻烏頭門，复漳城，馳大埔，郭揚維率四千人降，乘勝克南靖。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he intercepted Shixian at Anxi, advanced to attack Wutou Gate, recovered Zhangzhou, galloped to Dapu—Guo Yangwei led four thousand men to surrender—and pressed the victory to take Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he blocked Shixian at Anxi, retook Zhangzhou, raced to Dapu where Guo Yangwei surrendered four thousand men, and took Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 易勇號曰達衝阿，遷布政使。

translations.literal: His heroic title was changed to Dachong'a and he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His title became Dachong'a and he became administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十月，援嘉應，頓塔子墺，與諸軍環偪之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he aided Jiaying, encamped at Tazi'ao, and with the other armies surrounded and pressed the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he aided Jiaying, camped at Tazi'ao, and surrounded the enemy with allied forces.

sentences.zh: 追寇，寇返奔。

translations.literal: Pursuing the bandits, the bandits turned and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the bandits, they turned and ran.

sentences.zh: 時宗棠軍大埔，麾下止八百人，勢岌岌，亟召德榜扼三河壩。

translations.literal: At that time Zongtang's army was at Dapu with only eight hundred men under him—the situation was perilous—and he urgently summoned Debang to hold Sanheba.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang at Dapu had only eight hundred men in peril and urgently summoned Debang to Sanheba.

sentences.zh: 地當潮州要衝，皆山道絕澗。

translations.literal: The place stood at the critical pass of Chaozhou, all mountain roads and sheer ravines.
translations.idiomatic: It guarded Chaozhou's vital pass amid mountains and ravines.

sentences.zh: 德榜至，察地勢，度寇必不往，且主帥軍孤懸，寇直犯必不支，乃請當中路，卒與典軍出寇前遏之。

translations.literal: When Debang arrived he surveyed the terrain, judged the bandits would not go that way, and that with the commander's army isolated a direct enemy strike could not be held; he asked to take the center route and in the end with Dian's army went before the bandits to block them.
translations.idiomatic: Debang saw the enemy would not come that way, feared for Zongtang's isolated force, took the center, and with Liu Dian blocked the bandits ahead.

sentences.zh: 十二月，复嘉應，誅海洋。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jiaying was recovered and Haiyang was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jiaying fell and Haiyang was executed.

sentences.zh: 捷入，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Victory brought a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 六年，遭父憂歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he returned on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he went home for his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 十年八月，宗棠徵河州回，德榜詣軍所綜營務。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year Zongtang campaigned against the Hezhou Hui; Debang went to headquarters to manage overall affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, eighth month, Zongtang campaigned against Hezhou Hui; Debang managed headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 時黑山壘林立，勢張甚。

translations.literal: At that time Heishan stockades stood thickly and their power was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Heishan forts stood thick and strong.

sentences.zh: 德榜率二千人自狄道渡洮，以石鼓墩左拂黑山，右扼邊家灣，形便控駕，乃築二壘其上，與諸軍痛擊，寇壘悉平。

translations.literal: Debang led two thousand men from Didao across the Tao, with Shigudun on the left brushing Heishan and on the right holding Bianjiawan—the terrain advantageous for control—and built two stockades on it; together with the armies he struck hard and all bandit stockades were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He led two thousand from Didao across the Tao, flanked Heishan from Shigudun, held Bianjiawan, built two forts, and cleared every bandit stockade.

sentences.zh: 進駐迤南三甲集，率騎越山南下，大破之。

translations.literal: Advancing to garrison Yinan Sanjiaji, he led cavalry over the mountains southward and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Yinan Sanjiaji, led cavalry over the mountains south, and won greatly.

sentences.zh: 剿東鄉，抵陰窪泉，遇伏，下馬督戰，寇潰。

translations.literal: Campaigning in Dongxiang he reached Yinwaquan, met an ambush, dismounted to direct the battle, and the bandits broke.
translations.idiomatic: In Dongxiang at Yinwaquan he met an ambush, fought on foot, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 迭克要害，寇併入謝家坪。

translations.literal: He captured critical points in succession and the bandits merged into Xiejiaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He took key points in turn until the bandits massed at Xiejiaoping.

sentences.zh: 十一年，傅先宗戰歿新路坡，德榜接統其軍，申明紀律，誅將弁先潰者六人，士氣復新。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Fu Xianzong died in battle at Xinlupo; Debang took over his army, declared discipline, executed six officers who fled first, and morale was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Fu Xianzong fell at Xinlupo; Debang took his army, executed six fleeing officers, and restored morale.

sentences.zh: 羌地曠，夙患狼，往往百十成群，夜入幕帳噬人。

translations.literal: The Qiang country is vast and wolves had long been a plague, often gathering in groups of a hundred or ten and at night entering tents to devour men.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang country is wide; wolves often ran in packs of dozens and entered tents at night.

sentences.zh: 德榜令將士習獵搜捕，狼患減。

translations.literal: Debang ordered officers and men to practice hunting and capture them, and the wolf plague diminished.
translations.idiomatic: He had troops hunt them and the wolf plague eased.

sentences.zh: 甘南既平，撫降回十餘萬。

translations.literal: When southern Gansu was pacified he pacified more than a hundred thousand surrendered Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When southern Gansu was pacified he settled over a hundred thousand surrendered Hui.

sentences.zh: 濬狄道河渠，獲沃壤百餘萬畝。

translations.literal: He dredged the Didao canals and gained more than a million mu of fertile land.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged Didao canals and opened more than a million mu of fertile land.

sentences.zh: 降敕褒嘉，賜頭品秩。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript praised him and he was granted the first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial praise brought the first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，母憂，解職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he went on his mother's mourning and left office.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year one his mother's mourning ended his service.

sentences.zh: 六年，再赴新疆，以舊部駐張家口。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he went to Xinjiang again and stationed his old troops at Zhangjiakou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he returned to Xinjiang with old troops at Zhangjiakou.

sentences.zh: 七年，入京，教練火器、健銳諸營，兼興畿輔水利。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered the capital, trained the firearms and Jianrui camps, and also promoted waterworks in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he entered Beijing, trained firearms and Jianrui camps, and promoted capital-region waterworks.

sentences.zh: 十年，越南事亟，率師赴難。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Vietnamese affair was urgent and he led his army to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Vietnamese crisis called him to the front.

sentences.zh: 抵龍州，募新軍八營，號定邊軍，單騎詣諒山，謁徐延旭陳方略。

translations.literal: Reaching Longzhou he recruited eight new battalions called the Dingbian Army, rode alone to Lang Son, and called on Xu Yanxu to present his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: At Longzhou he raised eight Dingbian battalions, rode alone to Lang Son, and laid strategy before Xu Yanxu.

sentences.zh: 令提督張春發分兵駐朝陽山、半隴山左右，何秀清等駐驅驢墟，通運道，而自領兵赴鎮南關。

translations.literal: He ordered Regional Commander Zhang Chunfa to divide troops garrisoning Chaoyang Mountain and the left and right of Banlong Mountain, He Xiuqing and others at Qulüxu to open supply routes, and himself led troops to Zhennan Pass.
