translations.idiomatic: He posted Zhang Chunfa on Chaoyang and Banlong hills, He Xiuqing at Qulüxu to open supply, and went to Zhennan Pass himself.

sentences.zh: 北寧陷，權廣西提督。

translations.literal: When Bac Ninh fell he acted as military governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Bac Ninh fell he acted as Guangxi military governor.

sentences.zh: 戰豐谷，敗，蘇元春不往援，德榜銜之；

translations.literal: At the battle of Fenggu he was defeated; Su Yuanchun did not come to his aid, and Debang bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated at Fenggu without Su Yuanchun's aid, Debang resented him.

sentences.zh: 以故元春敗於谷松，亦不往救。

translations.literal: For this reason when Yuanchun was defeated at Gusong he also did not go to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when Su was beaten at Gusong, Wang did not help either.

sentences.zh: 德榜自負湘中宿將，與督師不洽。

translations.literal: Debang, proud as an old Hunan veteran, was at odds with the commanding general.
translations.idiomatic: Proud as a Hunan veteran, Debang clashed with the commander.

sentences.zh: 潘鼎新責其戰不力，劾罷之，以所部屬元春。

translations.literal: Pan Dingxin blamed him for not fighting hard enough, memorialized for his dismissal, and assigned his troops to Yuanchun.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Dingxin blamed his fighting, had him dismissed, and gave his troops to Su.

sentences.zh: 九月，復被命赴那陽，進偪船頭，戰數捷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was again ordered to Nayang, advanced on Chuantou, and won several battles.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was sent to Nayang, pressed Chuantou, and won repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 明年，軍油隘，法軍犯長牆，出師夾擊，據文淵對山，鏖戰數日，殺傷略相當。

translations.literal: The next year the army was at You'ai; the French attacked the long wall; the army went out in a pincer and held the hill opposite Van Tien; after several days of fierce fighting casualties were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Next year at You'ai the French hit the long wall; he pincered, held the hill opposite Van Tien, and fought for days with even losses.

sentences.zh: 越日，陳嘉爭東嶺三壘，德榜擊其背，克之。

translations.literal: The next day Chen Jia contested the three stockades on the eastern ridge; Debang struck their rear and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Chen Jia fought for the eastern ridge forts; Debang hit the rear and took them.

sentences.zh: 是日晨，出甫谷，敵援至，衝截為二，部將蕭得龍及春發戰最勇，殲法軍百餘人，獲糧械無算。

translations.literal: That morning, leaving Fugu Valley, enemy reinforcements arrived and cut them in two; subordinate Xiao Delong and Chunfa fought most bravely, killing more than a hundred French troops and capturing grain and arms beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: That morning leaving Fugu, reinforcements cut them in two; Xiao Delong and Chunfa fought hardest, killing over a hundred French and seizing vast stores.

sentences.zh: 敵被截，大潰。

translations.literal: The intercepted enemy broke completely.
translations.idiomatic: The cut-off enemy collapsed.

sentences.zh: 已，復合諸軍攻諒城，法軍扼驅驢墟，地故有德榜舊壘，堅且緻。

translations.literal: Presently the combined armies again attacked Lang Son; the French held Qulüxu—there was an old stockade of Debang's, strong and well built.
translations.idiomatic: The allies attacked Lang Son; the French held Qulüxu at Debang's old strong fort.

sentences.zh: 平明，德榜殲其六畫兵總一，諸軍繼之，城复。

translations.literal: At daybreak Debang killed one six-stripe company commander; the other armies followed and the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Debang killed a six-stripe commander; the allies followed and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 谷松敵勢仍悍，又殲其三畫兵總一，於是法人大潰，悉返侵地。

translations.literal: The enemy at Gusong was still fierce; he again killed one three-stripe company commander, and thereupon the French broke completely and wholly restored the invaded territory.
translations.idiomatic: At Gusong he killed a three-stripe commander; the French then collapsed and all occupied land was recovered.

sentences.zh: 復故官，被賞賚。

translations.literal: He recovered his former office and received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He regained his rank and received rewards.

sentences.zh: 尋移疾​​去。

translations.literal: Soon he left on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he retired ill.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授貴州布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed provincial administration commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became Guizhou administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十九年，卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died; condolence gifts followed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he died; mourning honors followed statute.

sentences.zh: 張春發，字蘭陔，江西新喻人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chunfa, style name Lanhai, was a native of Xinyu in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chunfa, courtesy name Lanhai, came from Xinyu in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 初隸劉松山麾下，充探騎，頻有功。

translations.literal: At first he served under Liu Songshan as a scout and won frequent merit.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Liu Songshan as scout and won frequent merit.

sentences.zh: 累遷至副將，賜號傑勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several steps to vice commander and granted the title Jieyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice commander and received Jieyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 從征陝回，規寧靈，戰常陷堅，擢總兵。

translations.literal: Campaigning against the Shaanxi Hui he aimed at Ning and Ling; in battle he often broke the hard places and was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Against Shaanxi Hui he targeted Ning and Ling, often broke the hard points, and became regional commander.

sentences.zh: 金積堡寇決渠淹我師，春發開溝築堤，引流反灌，破壘二百餘，更勇號曰哲爾精阿。

translations.literal: At Jinchengbao the bandits breached canals to flood our army; Chunfa opened ditches and built dikes, diverted water to flood back, broke more than two hundred stockades, and his heroic title was changed to Zhe'erjing'a.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinchengbao rebels flooded the army; Zhang counter-flooded, broke two hundred forts, and received the title Zhe'erjing'a.

sentences.zh: 复巴燕戎格及河州，晉提督。

translations.literal: He recovered Bayan Rongge and Hezhou and was advanced to military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Bayan Rongge and Hezhou and became military governor.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，從劉錦棠取迪化，連克瑪納斯、達坂、托克遜，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he followed Liu Jintang in taking Dihua and in succession captured Manas, Daban, and Toksun, and was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year two he followed Liu Jintang to take Dihua, Manas, Daban, and Toksun, and received a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 進復西四城，予世職。

translations.literal: Advancing, he recovered the four western cities and was granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered the four western cities and received a hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，安集延布魯特入寇，春發度幕趨博斯塘特勒克，搗其巢，逐北至俄境。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Andijan and Burut tribes invaded; Chunfa crossed the desert toward Bostan Telek, struck their nest, and pursued north to the Russian border.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Andijan Buruts invaded; Zhang crossed the desert, smashed their base, and pursued to the Russian border.

sentences.zh: 法越肇釁，從德榜奪東嶺。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese conflict began he followed Debang in taking the eastern ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French War began he followed Wang Debang in taking the eastern ridge.

sentences.zh: 法援大集，彈入右額，貫左頰，裹創力戰，大捷。

translations.literal: French reinforcements massed; a bullet entered his right forehead and passed through his left cheek; he bound his wounds and fought on hard and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: French reinforcements massed; a ball through right brow and left cheek—he bound up, fought on, and won greatly.

sentences.zh: 除廣西右江鎮總兵，署廣東陸路提督，賞雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: He was appointed regional commander of Youjiang in Guangxi, acted as land-route military governor of Guangdong, and was rewarded with double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: He became Youjiang regional commander, acted as Guangdong land-route governor, and received double peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，平永安、長樂匪，予實授。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he pacified bandits in Yong'an and Changle and received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he pacified Yong'an and Changle bandits and received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，調湖北，逾歲，徙雲南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to Hubei; after a year he moved to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he went to Hubei; a year later to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 魏光燾劾其營務廢弛，論戍。

translations.literal: Wei Guangtao memorialized that his camp affairs were neglected and he was sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guangtao accused him of slack camp management and he was sentenced to exile.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，張之洞白其誣，复官，綜兩江營務。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year Zhang Zhidong cleared him of false charges, restored his office, and put him in charge of military affairs in the two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year Zhang Zhidong cleared the false charge, restored him, and gave him two-Jiang military affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，病免，旋卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong he was dismissed on illness and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong year three illness ended his service and he soon died.

sentences.zh: 春發治軍嚴，嘗云兵佚則驕惰，以故朝夕躬訓練，暇輒使濬河流，平道路。

translations.literal: Chunfa was strict in governing troops and used to say that idle soldiers grow proud and lazy; therefore morning and evening he personally trained them, and in leisure made them dredge rivers and level roads.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfa ran a strict camp: idle troops grow soft, so he drilled them daily and set them to dredging rivers and leveling roads.

sentences.zh: 然木訥寡文，疏酬應，同官先施者恆不答禮，且往往氣凌其上，卒以此叢忌。

translations.literal: Yet he was dull and poor in letters, careless in social exchange; when colleagues showed kindness first he often did not return courtesy, and often overbore his superiors in manner—thus in the end he drew many resentments.
translations.idiomatic: Dull and awkward in society, he often snubbed colleagues and overbore superiors, and so earned many enemies.

sentences.zh: 蕭得龍，籍湖南藍山。

translations.literal: Xiao Delong was registered in Lanshan, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Delong was registered at Lanshan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從援贛、浙，積勳至提督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign he followed campaigns to aid Jiangxi and Zhejiang, accumulated merit to military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng he aided Jiangxi and Zhejiang and rose to military governor.

sentences.zh: 調赴閩，克南陽、漳州。

translations.literal: Transferred to Fujian, he captured Nanyang and Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Fujian he took Nanyang and Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 攻嘉應，寇遁，追扼北溪，大敗之，賜號博奇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Attacking Jiaying, the bandits fled; he pursued and blocked them at Beixi and inflicted a great defeat, and was granted the title Boqi Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiaying he routed the enemy at Beixi and received Boqi Batulu.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，移師甘肅，克東鄉太子寺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he moved his army to Gansu and captured Dongxiang Taizi Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu he went to Gansu and took Dongxiang Taizi Temple.

sentences.zh: 越事危棘，與法人戰南關，殺傷略相當，奪東嶺三壘。

translations.literal: When the Vietnamese affair was perilous he fought the French at the southern pass; casualties were roughly equal and he took the three stockades on the eastern ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the Vietnamese crisis he fought at the southern pass with even losses and took three eastern-ridge forts.

sentences.zh: 功最，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: His merit was greatest and he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: His merit ranked first and he received a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 事寧，署莊浪協副將。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he acted as assistant regional commander of Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he acted as Zhuanglang assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 創發，卒於官，予優恤。

translations.literal: His wounds reopened and he died in office; generous condolence was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His wounds reopened; he died in office with generous mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 馬維騏，字介堂，雲南阿迷人。

translations.literal: Ma Weiqi, style name Jietang, was a native of the Aimi people in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Weiqi, courtesy name Jietang, was an Aimi native of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 少從岑毓英軍徵回寇，積功至都司，捕盜尤有名。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Cen Yuying's army against Hui rebels, accumulated merit to battalion commander, and was especially famed for capturing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Young he served Cen Yuying against Hui rebels, rose to battalion commander, and was famed for catching bandits.

sentences.zh: 越南事亟，又從毓英出關，以偏裨當一路。

translations.literal: When the Vietnamese affair grew urgent he again followed Yuying beyond the pass, commanding one route as a subordinate general.
translations.idiomatic: When Vietnam grew urgent he again followed Yuying beyond the pass on an independent column.

sentences.zh: 法越之戰，滇軍多有功，而以維騏及覃修綱、吳永安為著。

translations.literal: In the Franco-Vietnamese war the Yunnan army won much merit, and Weiqi together with Tan Xiugang and Wu Yong'an were most noted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sino-French War the Yunnan army shone, especially Ma Weiqi, Tan Xiugang, and Wu Yongan.

sentences.zh: 師攻宣光，垂克，法援大集，圍劉永福軍，維騏銳身馳救，鏖戰二晝夜，擊卻之。

translations.literal: The army attacked Xuanguang and was on the verge of taking it when French reinforcements massed and surrounded Liu Yongfu's army; Weiqi rushed to the rescue with elite troops, fought two days and nights, and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanguang, as the city was nearly taken, French reinforcements surrounded Liu Yongfu; Ma rushed with picked troops, fought two days and nights, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 從攻臨洮，功最，遷副將，賜號博多歡巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Linzhou with greatest merit, was transferred to vice commander, and granted the title Bodohuan Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: At Linzhou his merit ranked first; he became vice commander and received Bodohuan Batulu.

sentences.zh: 光緒十三年，襲攻倮黑，間道濟瀾滄江。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Guangxu he raided Luohai by surprise and crossed the Lancang River by a side path.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year thirteen he raided Luohai, crossing the Lancang by a hidden path.

sentences.zh: 賊驚潰，斬其酋張登發，闢地千里，晉總兵。

translations.literal: The bandits fled in alarm; he beheaded their chief Zhang Dengfa, opened a thousand li of territory, and was advanced to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits broke; he killed chief Zhang Dengfa, opened a thousand li of ground, and became regional commander.

sentences.zh: 頻年越匪亂，騷擾各州邑，設方略治之，邊境以安。

translations.literal: For years Vietnamese bandits had disturbed the prefectures; he set strategy to govern them and the border was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: For years Vietnamese bandits had raided the districts; his strategy pacified the border.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，除廣東潮州鎮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed commander of Chaozhou in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he became Chaozhou commander in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 越四年，擢四川提督。

translations.literal: Four years later he was promoted to military governor of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Four years on he became Sichuan military governor.

sentences.zh: 仁壽、彭山土寇起，焚教堂，殺教民，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Renshou and Pengshan, burned churches, and killed Catholic converts—the momentum was fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou and Pengshan bandits burned churches and killed converts in a violent rising.

sentences.zh: 岑春煊諗其嫺武略，軍事一以屬之，用兵數月，以次戡定。

translations.literal: Cen Chunxuan knew his skill in military affairs and entrusted all military matters to him; within months he pacified them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Chunxuan gave him full military charge; within months he suppressed the rising.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，打箭爐關外泰凝寺喇嘛謀叛，率師討平之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year lamas of Taining Temple beyond Dajianlu plotted rebellion; he led troops to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year Taining Temple lamas beyond Dajianlu rebelled; he crushed them.

sentences.zh: 會巴塘蠢動，殺駐藏大臣鳳全，川邊大震。

translations.literal: Presently Batang stirred foolishly and killed the resident minister in Tibet Feng Quan; the Sichuan frontier was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Then Batang rose, killed Resident Minister Feng Quan in Tibet, and shook the Sichuan frontier.

sentences.zh: 維騏剿撫兼施，克要害，擒渠率，賜頭品秩、黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Weiqi combined suppression and pacification, took critical points, captured ringleaders, and was granted the first-rank cap button and yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Ma combined force and conciliation, took key points, captured chiefs, and received the first-rank button and yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 趙爾巽督川，改編巡防軍，奏充翼長，訓練士卒，創設將弁學堂，軍民綏戢。

translations.literal: When Zhao Erxun governed Sichuan he reorganized the patrol army, memorialized Weiqi as wing commander, trained troops, and founded an officers' academy—the army and people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhao Erxun he reorganized patrol forces, trained troops, founded an officers' school, and pacified army and people.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he died; condolence gifts followed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong year two he died; mourning honors followed statute.

sentences.zh: 覃修綱，籍廣西西林。

translations.literal: Tan Xiugang was registered in Xilin, Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Xiugang was registered at Xilin in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 隸毓英麾下，與維騏齊名。

translations.literal: He served under Yuying and was as famed as Weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuying he was as famed as Ma Weiqi.

sentences.zh: 徵回有功，累遷至參將，賜號勤勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: For merit against the Hui he was promoted through several steps to regimental commander and granted the title Qinyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Against the Hui he rose to regimental commander and received Qinyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 從克雲州，晉副將，更勇號曰隆武。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Yunzhou, was advanced to vice commander, and his heroic title was changed to Longwu.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Yunzhou, became vice commander, and his title became Longwu.

sentences.zh: 宣光之役，修綱獨扼夏和、清波，分兵取嘉喻關，复招越民九千，分頓要隘，綴法軍。

translations.literal: In the Xuanguang campaign Xiugang alone held Xiahe and Qingbo, detached troops to take Jiayu Pass, also recruited nine thousand Vietnamese, stationed them at critical passes, and pinned the French army.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanguang Tan held Xiahe and Qingbo, took Jiayu Pass, recruited nine thousand Vietnamese to critical posts, and pinned the French.

sentences.zh: 緬旺前接山西、興化，後達十州、三猛，為敵所據，出不意襲克之。

translations.literal: Mianwang fronted Shanxi and Xinghua and reached the ten prefectures and Sanmeng in the rear; the enemy held it—he struck unexpectedly and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Mianwang linked Shanxi and Xinghua to the rear ten prefectures; he surprised and took it.

sentences.zh: 次年，永福戰失利，軍潰退，修綱仍堅持不動。

translations.literal: The next year Yongfu was defeated in battle and the army routed and withdrew, yet Xiugang still held firm without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Yongfu was beaten and the army routed, yet Tan held his ground.

sentences.zh: 戰臨洮，斬其二將，夜半時，率死士短兵搏擊，法人大敗。

translations.literal: At the battle of Linzhou he beheaded two of their generals; at midnight he led picked men in close combat and the French were badly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Linzhou he killed two French generals; at midnight picked men routed them in close fight.

sentences.zh: 乘勝复各郡縣，北圻諸省皆響應。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory he recovered the prefectures and counties in succession, and all the northern Tonkin provinces responded.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered prefecture after prefecture and all northern Tonkin answered.

sentences.zh: 修綱出奇兵直搗越南中部，而奉命罷戍。

translations.literal: Xiugang sent raiding troops straight into central Vietnam, but orders came to cease campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: Tan sent raiders into central Vietnam, but ceasefire orders arrived.

sentences.zh: 事寧，賞黃馬褂，署川北鎮總兵，仍留滇。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket, acted as regional commander of Chuanbei, and remained in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he received a yellow jacket, acted as Chuanbei commander, and stayed in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 歷權普洱、開化諸鎮，坐事免。

translations.literal: He successively acted at Pu'er and Kaihua and was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He acted at Pu'er and Kaihua in turn and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十五年，起甘肅西寧鎮，留滇如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Guangxu he was reinstated at Xining in Gansu but remained in Yunnan as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year twenty-five he was restored at Xining but stayed in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，卒，予建祠，並毓英祠附祀。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he died; permission to build a temple was granted, with joint worship at Yuying's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he died; a temple was granted with worship at Yuying's shrine.

sentences.zh: 修綱性忠勇，官開化久，有惠政，士民感頌，因寄籍文山雲。

translations.literal: Xiugang was loyal and brave; he long governed Kaihua with benevolent policy, and officers and people praised him—thus he registered domicile at Wenshan.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and brave, Tan long governed Kaihua with kindness; the people praised him and he registered at Wenshan.

sentences.zh: 吳永安，籍雲南廣西州。

translations.literal: Wu Yong'an was registered in Guangxi prefecture, Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yongan was registered at Guangxi prefecture in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 毓英部將中稱驍果。

translations.literal: Among Yuying's subordinate generals he was called the fiercest and most resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Among Yuying's generals he was called the boldest.

sentences.zh: 以徵回功，累遷至副將，賜號尚勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: For merit against the Hui he was promoted through several steps to vice commander and granted the title Shangyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Against the Hui he rose to vice commander and received Shangyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 從克澂江，擢總兵。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Chengjiang and was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Chengjiang and became regional commander.

sentences.zh: 平館驛，晉提督，更勇號曰額特和，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He pacified Guanyi post station, was advanced to military governor, his heroic title was changed to Etehe, and he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Guanyi, became military governor, title Etehe, and received a yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 毓英撫福建，奏署台灣鎮，未之官，憂歸。

translations.literal: When Yuying governed Fujian he memorialized Yong'an to act as Taiwan commander; he did not take the post and returned on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuying named him acting Taiwan commander in Fujian; mourning kept him from taking post.

sentences.zh: 起治雲南邊防。

translations.literal: He was recalled to manage Yunnan frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to manage Yunnan border defense.

sentences.zh: 法人浮小舟渡沱江，永安乘其半濟，擊敗之。

translations.literal: The French floated small boats to cross the Tuojiang; Yong'an struck them halfway across and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: French boats crossed the Tuojiang; Wu struck them half over and won.

sentences.zh: 趨宣光，留三營扼守，而自間道還興化合岑軍。

translations.literal: He hurried to Xuanguang, left three battalions to hold the line, and by a side path returned to Xinghua to join Cen's army.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to Xuanguang, left three battalions, and by a hidden path rejoined Cen at Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 既而諸軍攻宣光，與修綱分扼要隘，取嘉喻關，攻臨洮，戰益利，予優敘。

translations.literal: Presently the armies attacked Xuanguang; with Xiugang he held critical passes in division, took Jiayu Pass, attacked Linzhou, and fighting grew more favorable; he received preferential recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Then at Xuanguang he and Tan held passes, took Jiayu, attacked Linzhou with growing success, and received special honors.

sentences.zh: 和議成，署昭通鎮。

translations.literal: When peace was made he acted as commander of Zhaotong.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he acted as Zhaotong commander.

sentences.zh: 討平武定夷匪，補鶴麗鎮。

translations.literal: He campaigned against and pacified Yi bandits in Wuding and was appointed to Heli command.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed Wuding Yi bandits and was posted to Heli.

sentences.zh: 光緒十九年，卒，附祀毓英祠。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Guangxu he died; joint worship at Yuying's temple was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year nineteen he died with worship at Yuying's shrine.

sentences.zh: 孫開華，字賡堂，湖南慈利人。

translations.literal: Sun Kaihua, style name Gengtang, was a native of Cili in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kaihua, courtesy name Gengtang, came from Cili in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 少從軍，從鮑超援江西，戰九江小池口，傷右臂。

translations.literal: In youth he joined the army; he followed Bao Chao to aid Jiangxi and fought at Jiujiang and Xiaochikou, wounding his right arm.
translations.idiomatic: Young he joined the army, followed Bao Chao in Jiangxi at Jiujiang and Xiaochikou, and wounded his right arm.

sentences.zh: 援湖北，再被創。

translations.literal: Aiding Hubei he was wounded again.
translations.idiomatic: Aiding Hubei he was wounded again.

sentences.zh: 池驛之役，夾擊敗敵，積勳至守備。

translations.literal: At the battle of Chiyi he struck the enemy in a pincer and defeated them, accumulating merit to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Chiyi he pincered and beat the enemy and rose to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 同治初，轉戰皖、贛間，遷副將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign he campaigned between Anhui and Jiangxi and was transferred to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi he fought in Anhui and Jiangxi and became vice commander.

sentences.zh: 克句容、金壇，賜號擢勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He captured Jurong and Jintan and was granted the title Zhuoyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jurong and Jintan and received Zhuoyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 以次攻金溪、南豐、新城、寧都、瑞金，並下之，晉總兵。

translations.literal: In succession he attacked and took Jinxi, Nanfeng, Xincheng, Ningdu, and Ruijin, and was advanced to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jinxi, Nanfeng, Xincheng, Ningdu, and Ruijin in turn and became regional commander.

sentences.zh: 廣東，嘉應亂，敗賊黃沙嶂，降者十餘萬，擢提督。

translations.literal: In Guangdong, when Jiaying was in revolt, he defeated the bandits at Huangshazhang and more than a hundred thousand surrendered; he was promoted to military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong he beat Jiaying rebels at Huangshazhang; over a hundred thousand surrendered and he became governor.

sentences.zh: 五年，除漳州鎮總兵，仍北行追捻入楚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed regional commander of Zhangzhou and still marched north pursuing the Nian into Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became Zhangzhou commander and still pursued the Nian north into Hubei.

sentences.zh: 其秋，赴本官。

translations.literal: That autumn he went to his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he took up his regular post.

sentences.zh: 總督文煜累疏薦其才。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wen Yu repeatedly memorialized recommending his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wen Yu repeatedly praised his talent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，總督李宗羲治江防，設霆慶、霆匯諸營。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Governor-General Li Zongyi managed Yangtze defenses and established the Tingqing and Tinghui battalions.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Li Zongyi organized Yangtze defense with Tingqing and Tinghui battalions.

sentences.zh: 廈門與台、澎對峙，勢險要，開華以超舊將，被命治廈門海防。

translations.literal: Xiamen faced Taiwan and Penghu across the strait—the terrain critical; Kaihua as an old subordinate of Bao was ordered to manage Xiamen coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: Xiamen faced Taiwan and Penghu; as Bao Chao's old officer Sun was ordered to defend Xiamen's coast.

sentences.zh: 募勇成捷勝軍，赴台北、蘇澳營辦開山，詔署陸路提督。

translations.literal: He recruited troops to form the Jiesheng Army, went to Taipei and Suao to open mountains lands, and was ordered to act as land-route military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the Jiesheng Army, opened lands at Taipei and Suao, and acted as land-route governor.

sentences.zh: 十年，法人來犯，時劉銘傳主軍事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the French came to attack; at that time Liu Mingchuan commanded military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the French attacked; Liu Mingchuan commanded.

sentences.zh: 銘傳故淮軍宿將，知開華幹略，檄守滬尾。

translations.literal: Mingchuan was an old Huai Army general and knew Kaihua's ability; he ordered him to defend Huwei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, an old Huai general, knew Sun's skill and ordered him to hold Huwei.

sentences.zh: 初，法艦八艘至，開華度其必登岸，令諸將分伏砲台後，露宿以待。

translations.literal: At first eight French warships arrived; Kaihua judged they would land and ordered the generals to lie in ambush behind the batteries and camp in the open awaiting them.
translations.idiomatic: Eight French ships came; Sun expected a landing, hid men behind the batteries, and waited overnight.

sentences.zh: 部署甫定，而敵彈雨坌，煙焰翳天，偪台而前。

translations.literal: The deployment was just set when enemy shells fell like rain, smoke veiled the sky, and they pressed the fort.
translations.idiomatic: As his dispositions settled, shells rained, smoke filled the sky, and the enemy pressed the fort.

sentences.zh: 開華見勢猛，分路截擊，自夜至午，卻而復前者數四。

translations.literal: Kaihua saw the momentum was fierce and struck by separate routes from night till noon; they fell back and came on again four times.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing fierce pressure, Sun counterattacked by separate routes from night to noon four times.

sentences.zh: 台既毀，短兵接戰。

translations.literal: The fort was destroyed and they fought hand to hand.
translations.idiomatic: The fort fell and they fought hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 開華銳身入，手刃執旗卒，奪其旗以歸。

translations.literal: Kaihua charged in himself, personally killed the standard-bearer, and seized the flag to return.
translations.idiomatic: Sun charged in, killed the standard-bearer, and seized the flag.

sentences.zh: 諸軍士見之，氣益奮，斬馘二千餘級，法人遁走。

translations.literal: The soldiers seeing this were still more roused; more than two thousand heads were cut and the French fled.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were stirred to cut over two thousand heads and drive the French off.

sentences.zh: 歐洲諸國以失國旗為至辱。

translations.literal: European countries regard the loss of a national flag as the utmost disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: European nations regard losing a national flag as ultimate disgrace.

sentences.zh: 捷入，予世職，拜幫辦軍務之命。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was granted a hereditary office and appointed to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Victory brought a hereditary rank and appointment to assist military affairs.

sentences.zh: 和議成，還本官，旋予實授。

translations.literal: When peace was made he returned to his regular post and soon received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he returned to his post and soon received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 十九年，卒，諡壯武。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died; posthumous title Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he died, posthumous name Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 子道仁，亦官福建提督。

translations.literal: His son Daoren also held the post of military governor of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoren also became Fujian military governor.

sentences.zh: 同時守滬尾者，硃煥明為最著。

translations.literal: Of those who defended Huwei at the same time, Zhu Huanming was most noted.
translations.idiomatic: Among Huwei's defenders Zhu Huanming was most noted.

sentences.zh: 煥明，籍安徽合肥。

translations.literal: Huanming was registered in Hefei, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huanming was registered at Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初從銘軍徵粵寇，積功至游擊。

translations.literal: At first he followed the Ming Army against Cantonese rebels and accumulated merit to mobile corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed the Ming Army against Cantonese rebels and rose to mobile corps commander.

sentences.zh: 平東捻，遷副將。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were pacified he was transferred to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern Nian were pacified he became vice commander.

sentences.zh: 西捻犯畿疆，躡之滄州、德平，戰數利，晉總兵。

translations.literal: When the western Nian raided the capital region he pursued them to Cangzhou and Dezhou and won several battles, and was advanced to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When western Nian raided the capital region he pursued them to Cangzhou and Dezhou and became regional commander.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，台灣生番騷動，從唐定奎往討，連破竹坑山、內外獅頭，擢提督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu aboriginals in Taiwan stirred; he followed Tang Dingkui to suppress them, successively broke Zhukeng Mountain and inner and outer Shitou, and was promoted to military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year one he followed Tang Dingkui against Taiwan aborigines, took Zhukeng and Shitou, and became military governor.

sentences.zh: 法越之役，法軍分道犯滬尾。

translations.literal: In the Franco-Vietnamese war the French army came by separate routes to attack Huwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sino-French War French columns attacked Huwei.

sentences.zh: 煥明當北路，被重創，戰益力，開華直入擊退之。

translations.literal: Huanming held the north route, was gravely wounded, and fought all the harder; Kaihua charged straight in and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Huanming held the north, was badly wounded, fought harder; Sun charged in and drove the French back.

sentences.zh: 旋移師台北，平番社，軍嘉義鹿港。

translations.literal: Soon he moved his army to Taipei, pacified aboriginal villages, and garrisoned Lugang in Jiayi.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Taipei, pacified aboriginal villages, and garrisoned Lugang in Jiayi.

sentences.zh: 土寇數千薄城，煥明率三百人與戰，殞於陣。

translations.literal: Several thousand local bandits pressed the city; Huanming led three hundred men to fight and fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of bandits pressed the city; Zhu led three hundred men and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 事聞，附祀定奎祠。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, joint worship at Dingkui's temple was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him joint worship at Tang Dingkui's shrine.

sentences.zh: 蘇得勝，亦籍合肥。

translations.literal: Su Desheng was also registered in Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Su Desheng was also registered at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 從銘軍討捻，積功至游擊。

translations.literal: He followed the Ming Army against the Nian, accumulated merit to mobile corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Ming Army against the Nian and rose to mobile corps commander.

sentences.zh: 戰常陷堅，賜號勵勇巴圖魯，屢遷提督。

translations.literal: In battle he often broke the hard places and was granted the title Liyong Batulu; he was promoted several times to military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He often broke the hard points, received Liyong Batulu, and rose repeatedly to military governor.

sentences.zh: 法艦寇台灣，從銘傳守台北。

translations.literal: When French warships raided Taiwan he followed Mingchuan to defend Taipei.
translations.idiomatic: When French ships raided Taiwan he defended Taipei under Liu Mingchuan.

sentences.zh: 戰基隆，大捷，記名海疆總兵，更勇號曰西林。

translations.literal: At the battle of Keelung he won a great victory, was recorded as coastal regional commander, and his heroic title was changed to Xilin.
translations.idiomatic: At Keelung he won greatly, was named coastal regional commander, and his title became Xilin.

sentences.zh: 滬尾告警，銘軍回援，於是基隆再失。

translations.literal: When Huwei sounded the alarm the Ming Army returned to aid, and thereupon Keelung was lost again.
translations.idiomatic: When Huwei was threatened the Ming Army returned to aid and Keelung fell again.

sentences.zh: 逮滬尾既复，得勝還駐六堵。

translations.literal: When Huwei was recovered Desheng returned to garrison Liudu.
translations.idiomatic: After Huwei was saved Su returned to garrison Liudu.

sentences.zh: 規基隆，全軍會月眉山，曹志忠將左，劉朝祐將右，得勝居中。

translations.literal: Planning Keelung, the whole army assembled at Yuemeishan; Cao Zhizhong commanded the left, Liu Chaoyou the right, and Desheng the center.
translations.idiomatic: To retake Keelung the army assembled at Yuemeishan: Cao Zhizhong left, Liu Chaoyou right, Su center.

sentences.zh: 敵至左路，擊卻之。

translations.literal: The enemy came on the left route and was driven back.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy hit the left and was repulsed.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，法益兵攻志忠營，得勝領數百人往援，戰失利，提督梁善明陣亡，右師亦潰，月眉復不守。

translations.literal: After a year the French increased troops and attacked Zhizhong's camp; Desheng led several hundred men to aid, the battle went badly, Military Governor Liang Shanming died in battle, the right wing also broke, and Yuemei was lost again.
translations.idiomatic: A year on the French reinforced, Su aided Cao with hundreds, Liang Shanming fell, the right broke, and Yuemei was lost again.

sentences.zh: 而得勝已先營六堵，築城十餘裡，諸軍獲安。

translations.literal: But Desheng had already built Liudu beforehand, constructing a city of more than ten li, and the armies were secure.
translations.idiomatic: Su had already fortified Liudu with a ten-li wall and kept the armies safe.

sentences.zh: 相持月餘，和議成，始開港。

translations.literal: After holding more than a month peace was made and the port was opened.
translations.idiomatic: After a month of stalemate peace came and the port opened.

sentences.zh: 旋補建寧鎮，仍留防滬尾。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed to Jianning command but remained to defend Huwei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posted to Jianning but stayed to defend Huwei.

sentences.zh: 數剿生番，感瘴成疾。

translations.literal: He campaigned several times against aborigines and contracted malaria.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated aboriginal campaigns brought malaria.

sentences.zh: 光緒十六年，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Guangxu he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year sixteen he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 妻徐氏，絕食殉焉。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Xu starved herself to death in martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Xu starved herself in martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 卹如製，妻獲旌。

translations.literal: Condolence followed regulation and the wife received an imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning followed statute and his wife was honored.

sentences.zh: 章高元，亦合肥人。

translations.literal: Zhang Gaoyuan was also from Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gaoyuan was also from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 初入淮軍，累至副將。

translations.literal: He first entered the Huai Army and rose through several steps to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Huai Army and rose to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 銘傳檄為騎旅先鋒，轉戰魯、皖。

translations.literal: Mingchuan ordered him as vanguard of the cavalry brigade and he campaigned in Shandong and Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mingchuan made him cavalry vanguard in Shandong and Anhui.

sentences.zh: 安丘之役，以功擢總兵，賜號奇車巴圖魯。

translations.literal: At the battle of Anqiu he was promoted to regional commander for merit and granted the title Qiche Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: At Anqiu he became regional commander and received Qiche Batulu.

sentences.zh: 徵台灣，晉提督。

translations.literal: Campaigning in Taiwan he was advanced to military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiwan campaign he became military governor.

sentences.zh: 法越事作，署澎湖鎮總兵，銘傳檄援滬尾。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose he acted as regional commander of Penghu; Mingchuan ordered him to aid Huwei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French crisis broke out he acted at Penghu and was sent to aid Huwei.

sentences.zh: 滬尾、基隆既复，論功，更勇號年昌阿，除登萊青鎮。

translations.literal: When Huwei and Keelung were recovered, for merit his heroic title was changed to Nianchang'a and he was appointed to Denglaiqing command.
translations.idiomatic: After Huwei and Keelung were recovered his title became Nianchang'a and he took Denglaiqing command.

sentences.zh: 中日失和，詔赴前敵，駐蓋平。

translations.literal: When China and Japan fell out he was ordered to the front and garrisoned Gaiping.
translations.idiomatic: When war with Japan broke out he was sent to the front at Gaiping.

sentences.zh: 日軍來攻，戰挫遂退。

translations.literal: The Japanese came to attack; defeated in battle he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese attacked; beaten, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 德軍艦襲膠澳，被幽，旋脫歸，稱疾罷。

translations.literal: When German warships seized Jiaozhou he was detained but soon escaped and pleaded illness to resign.
translations.idiomatic: When Germany seized Jiaozhou he was held, escaped, and resigned ill.

sentences.zh: 拳亂作，起署天津鎮，徙重慶，以病免。

translations.literal: When the Boxer rising occurred he was recalled to act at Tianjin command, moved to Chongqing, and was dismissed on illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxers rose he acted at Tianjin, moved to Chongqing, and retired ill.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died aged seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 歐陽利見，字賡堂，湖南祁陽人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Lijian, style name Gengtang, was a native of Qiyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Lijian, courtesy name Gengtang, came from Qiyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，入長沙水師，轉戰贛、皖間，積功至游擊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign he entered the Changsha naval force and campaigned between Jiangxi and Anhui, accumulating merit to mobile corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng he joined the Changsha navy, fought in Jiangxi and Anhui, and rose to mobile corps commander.

sentences.zh: 同治改元，偽護王陳坤書據太平，以兵艦銜尾西上，環泊花洋上駟渡，期水陸並進。

translations.literal: When the Tongzhi reign began the false Protector King Chen Kunshu held Taiping; with warships tail to tail he sailed west and anchored at Huayang Shangsidu, planning a joint land-sea advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongzhi's start false Protector King Chen Kunshu held Taiping; his fleet anchored at Huayang Shangsidu for a joint land-sea attack.

sentences.zh: 利見領一軍為前鋒，兼程赴難。

translations.literal: Lijian led one army as vanguard and hurried day and night to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Lijian led a vanguard column day and night to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 坤書陽令陸路悍黨擊我師船，而陰結筏自下游竊渡。

translations.literal: Kunshu openly ordered fierce land forces to strike our ships while secretly joining rafts to cross downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Kunshu feigned a land attack on our ships while secretly rafting downstream.

sentences.zh: 利見诇知之，率所部長驅，乘風浪沖其筏為二。

translations.literal: Lijian learned of it, led his command in a long drive, and riding wind and waves smashed their rafts in two.
translations.idiomatic: Lijian learned this, raced up, and in wind and waves smashed the rafts in two.

sentences.zh: 寇大困，倚河築壘，矢堅守。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly distressed, leaned on the river to build stockades, and held firm with arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped, they built river stockades and held with arrows.

sentences.zh: 我師水陸分道進，利見駛入花山，擊其背。

translations.literal: Our army advanced by land and water in separate routes; Lijian sailed into Huashan and struck their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Land and water columns advanced; Lijian sailed into Huashan and hit their rear.

sentences.zh: 遲明，戰良久，寇陣不少動，援軍至，始退。

translations.literal: At dawn fighting lasted long yet the bandit line scarcely moved; when reinforcements arrived they at last withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the line held until reinforcements came and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 利見進次馬音街，會水師將李朝斌偪花津而陣，步騎助之，寇潰。

translations.literal: Lijian advanced to Mayin Street; the naval commander Li Chaobin pressed Huajin in formation with infantry and cavalry assisting, and the bandits broke.
translations.idiomatic: Lijian advanced to Mayin; Li Chaobin pressed Huajin with land support and the bandits broke.

sentences.zh: 翼日，复戰，陸師將周萬倬遇伏被創，利見銳身馳救，苦戰竟日，焚象山寇舍。

translations.literal: The next day fighting resumed; land commander Zhou Wanzhuo met an ambush and was wounded; Lijian rushed to the rescue with elite troops, fought bitterly all day, and burned the bandit lodges at Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Zhou Wanzhuo was ambushed; Lijian rushed to save him, fought all day, and burned Xiangshan lodges.

sentences.zh: 而寇艎聚泊小丹陽，歸護新市鎮。

translations.literal: The bandit ships gathered at Xiaodanyang and returned to protect Xinshi Town.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit ships gathered at Xiaodanyang and sheltered Xinshi.

sentences.zh: 利見進石臼湖轟擊之，獲其船十二艘，遷參將。

translations.literal: Lijian advanced to Shijiu Lake and bombarded them, capturing twelve of their boats, and was transferred to regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: He bombarded them at Shijiu Lake, took twelve boats, and became regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 二年，攻巢縣，偪城東門而軍，適彭毓橘軍至，燔其筏，毀浮橋。

translations.literal: In the second year he attacked Chaoxian, pressed the east gate of the city, and just then Peng Yujue's army arrived, burned their rafts, and destroyed the pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he pressed Chaoxian's east gate; Peng Yujue arrived, burned rafts, and destroyed the bridge.

sentences.zh: 寇入城，利見先登克之，遂與霆軍复含山。

translations.literal: The bandits entered the city; Lijian climbed first and took it, then with the Ting Army recovered Hanshan.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits entered the city; Lijian scaled first, took it, and with the Ting Army recovered Hanshan.

sentences.zh: 四日連下三城，功最，賜號強勇巴圖魯，調補狼山鎮游擊。

translations.literal: In four days he took three cities in succession; his merit was greatest and he was granted the title Qiangyong Batulu and transferred to fill the mobile corps commander post at Langshan.
translations.idiomatic: In four days he took three cities, received Qiangyong Batulu, and filled the Langshan mobile corps post.

sentences.zh: 克嘉定，遷副將。

translations.literal: He captured Jiading and was transferred to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jiading and became vice commander.

sentences.zh: 下太倉、崑山、新陽，晉總兵。

translations.literal: He took Taicang, Kunshan, and Xinyang and was advanced to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took Taicang, Kunshan, and Xinyang and became regional commander.

sentences.zh: 是時花涇港寇壘林立，與吳江、震澤寇相犄角。

translations.literal: At that time bandit stockades stood thick at Huajing Harbor, supporting each other with bandits at Wujiang and Zhenze.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit forts at Huajing Harbor supported Wujiang and Zhenze rebels.

sentences.zh: 利見率師破之，毀其船二十艘，城寇援絕乞降。

translations.literal: Lijian led his army to break them, destroyed twenty of their boats, and the city bandits, cut off from aid, begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Lijian broke them, destroyed twenty boats, and cut-off city bandits surrendered.

sentences.zh: 於是蘇、浙路梗，蘇寇無固志。

translations.literal: Thereupon the routes in Jiangsu and Zhejiang were blocked and Suzhou bandits lost firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu and Zhejiang routes were cut and Suzhou rebels lost heart.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章督師合圍，利見引兵從，迭克要害，寇宵遁。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang commanded the encirclement; Lijian led his troops in the follow-up, captured critical points in succession, and the bandits fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang encircled; Lijian followed, took key points, and the bandits fled by night.

sentences.zh: 城复，晉提督。

translations.literal: The city was recovered and he was advanced to military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell and he became military governor.

sentences.zh: 三年，攻嘉興，利見率謝世彩等與陸師夾擊，麾眾先登，自城上發巨砲轟之。

translations.literal: In the third year he attacked Jiaxing; Lijian led Xie Shicai and others to strike jointly with the land army, commanded the men to climb first, and from atop the wall fired great cannon to bombard them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year at Jiaxing he led Xie Shicai in a joint assault, climbed first, and fired great guns from the wall.

sentences.zh: 城寇駴亂，城遂拔。

translations.literal: The city bandits were thrown into alarm and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison panicked and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 以次下長興。

translations.literal: In succession he took Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Changxing.

sentences.zh: 坤書據常州，鴻章舉兵西，使利見造浮橋渡壕，四面環攻，坤書就擒。

translations.literal: Kunshu held Changzhou; Hongzhang raised troops westward, had Lijian build a pontoon bridge to cross the moat, attacked on four sides, and Kunshu was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Kunshu held Changzhou; Hongzhang attacked from four sides after Lijian bridged the moat, and Kunshu was captured.

sentences.zh: 中吳大定，除淮揚鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Central Wu was greatly settled and he was appointed regional commander of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Central Wu was settled and he became Huaiyang regional commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，捻至曲阜，東南走滕、嶧，渡運，東北走蘭山，南走郯，趨贛榆、青口，圖南下。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Nian reached Qufu, fled southeast to Teng and Yi, crossed the Grand Canal, fled northeast to Lanshan, south to Tan, and rushed Ganyu and Qingkou, intending to go south.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Nian reached Qufu, crossed the canal, and rushed south toward Ganyu and Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷憂裡下河，詔備淮揚防。

translations.literal: The court feared for the Lixiahe region and ordered defenses prepared at Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared for Lixiahe and ordered Huaiyang defenses.

sentences.zh: 於是利見率砲艦四十艘泊清江，兼治糈台。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lijian led forty gunboats to anchor at Qingjiang and also managed the grain depot.
translations.idiomatic: Lijian anchored forty gunboats at Qingjiang and managed the grain depot.

sentences.zh: 七年，黃河暴漲，利見乘流至德州，運防乃固。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Yellow River flooded violently; Lijian rode the current to Dezhou and transport defense was secured.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year floodwaters let him reach Dezhou and secure transport defense.

sentences.zh: 捻雖屢挫，然渡運之謀未已，盤旋河東上下。

translations.literal: Though the Nian were repeatedly beaten, their plan to cross the canal was not abandoned and they circled east and west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Though beaten often, the Nian still tried to cross the canal up and down its course.

sentences.zh: 利見復下駛援應，與諸軍環擊，捻益不支。

translations.literal: Lijian sailed down again in relief, joined the armies in encirclement, and the Nian grew still less able to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Lijian sailed down again, joined the encirclement, and the Nian weakened further.

sentences.zh: 事寧，賞黃馬褂，更勇號曰奇車伯。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket and his heroic title was changed to Qichebo.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he received a yellow jacket and the title Qichebo.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，調福山鎮。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was transferred to Fushan command.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year six he was posted to Fushan.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to military governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he became Zhejiang military governor.

sentences.zh: 十年，法艦寇福建，浙江戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the tenth year French warships raided Fujian and Zhejiang went on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year French ships raided Fujian and Zhejiang stood alert.

sentences.zh: 鎮海為浙東門戶，利見以三千五百人頓金雞山防南岸，提督楊岐珍以二千五百人頓招寶山防北岸，總兵錢玉興以三千五百人為游擊師。

translations.literal: Zhenhai was the gateway of eastern Zhejiang; Lijian stationed thirty-five hundred men at Jinji Mountain to defend the south bank, Military Governor Yang Qizhen thirty-five hundred at Zhaobao Mountain for the north bank, and Regional Commander Qian Yuxing thirty-five hundred as the mobile column.
translations.idiomatic: At gateway Zhenhai, Lijian held the south bank with 3,500 men, Yang Qizhen the north with 2,500, Qian Yuxing 3,500 as mobile reserve.

sentences.zh: 威遠、靖遠、鎮遠三砲台，守備吳杰領之，而元凱、超武二兵艦泊海口備策應。

translations.literal: The Weiyuan, Jingyuan, and Zhenyuan batteries were commanded by garrison commander Wu Jie, while the Yuankai and Chaowu gunboats anchored in the harbor for support.
translations.idiomatic: Batteries Weiyuan, Jingyuan, and Zhenyuan were under Wu Jie; Yuankai and Chaowu gunboats waited in the harbor.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆受利見節度。

translations.literal: All generals were under Lijian's command.
translations.idiomatic: All generals answered to Lijian.

sentences.zh: 利見實以兵備道薛福成為謀主，乃量形勢，設防禦，蒐軍實，清間諜，杜鄉導，申紀律，勵客將，布利器，部署甫定，而敵氛已偪。

translations.literal: Lijian in fact took defense intendant Xue Fucheng as his strategist; he then gauged terrain, set defenses, gathered military stores, cleared spies, cut off guides, enforced discipline, encouraged foreign officers, deployed sharp weapons—when deployment was just set the enemy was already pressing.
translations.idiomatic: He took Xue Fucheng as strategist, surveyed terrain, gathered stores, cleared spies, enforced discipline, deployed weapons—and as dispositions settled the enemy arrived.

sentences.zh: 法人狃馬江之役，頗輕浙防。

translations.literal: The French, emboldened by the Mawei affair, rather looked down on Zhejiang's defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by Mawei, the French underestimated Zhejiang's defense.

sentences.zh: 利見督台艦兵縱砲擊之，法主將坐船被傷，數以魚雷突入，皆被擊退。

translations.literal: Lijian directed the Taiwan fleet guns to bombard them; the French commander's flagship was hit, and several attempts to enter with torpedoes were all driven back.
translations.idiomatic: Lijian's shore guns hit the French flagship; torpedo attacks were repulsed.

sentences.zh: 法艦並力猛進，又沉其一。

translations.literal: The French warships advanced with combined strength and another was sunk.
translations.idiomatic: The French pressed together and lost another ship.

sentences.zh: 敵計窮，相持月餘，終不得逞。

translations.literal: The enemy's plans were exhausted; after holding more than a month they could not prevail in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy plans failed; after a month they could not break through.

sentences.zh: 事後知主將孤拔於是役殞焉。

translations.literal: Afterward it was learned that Commander Courbet fell in this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was learned that Admiral Courbet died in this fight.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其功，賜頭品秩。

translations.literal: The throne praised his merit and granted the first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised him and granted the first-rank button.

sentences.zh: 十五年，病免。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was dismissed on illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year illness ended his service.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，劉坤一被命援奉天，奏調利見赴軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Liu Kunyi was ordered to aid Fengtian and memorialized to transfer Lijian to the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Liu Kunyi was sent to aid Fengtian and called Lijian to the army.

sentences.zh: 力疾北行，卒於道，年七十一。

translations.literal: He forced himself north though ill and died on the road, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He forced himself north ill and died on the road at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 論曰：法越之役，克鎮南，复諒山，實為中西戰爭第一大捷。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the Franco-Vietnamese war, capturing Zhennan and recovering Lang Son was in truth the greatest victory in the wars between China and the West.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Taking Zhennan and recovering Lang Son was the greatest Sino-Western victory of the age.

sentences.zh: 摧強敵，揚國光，子材等之功也。

translations.literal: Crushing a strong enemy and raising national glory were the merit of Zicai and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Crushing a strong foe and raising national prestige were Feng Zicai and his comrades' achievement.

sentences.zh: 開華等復滬尾，利見等守鎮海，與維騏等偕劉永福之拔宣光，並傳榮譽。

translations.literal: Kaihua and others recovered Huwei, Lijian and others held Zhenhai, together with Weiqi and others joining Liu Yongfu in taking Xuanguang—all spread honor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun recovered Huwei, Ouyang held Zhenhai, Ma and Liu Yongfu took Xuanguang—all won glory.

sentences.zh: 當時挾戰勝之威，保台复越，亦尚有可為。

translations.literal: At that time, wielding the prestige of victory, securing Taiwan and recovering Vietnam were still possible.
translations.idiomatic: Then, riding victory's prestige, securing Taiwan and recovering Vietnam were still possible.

sentences.zh: 獨怪當事者為台灣難保之說以自餒其氣，致使關外雖利，而越南終非我有。

translations.literal: Only it is strange that those in charge preached that Taiwan could not be saved and so discouraged their own spirit, causing victory beyond the pass yet Vietnam in the end not to be ours.
translations.idiomatic: Yet leaders preached that Taiwan was lost and discouraged the nation, so border victories could not keep Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 罷戰詔下，軍民解體，至今聞者猶有恨焉。

translations.literal: When the ceasefire edict came down army and people dissolved; those who hear of it still harbor resentment to this day.
translations.idiomatic: When ceasefire came the army dissolved; resentment lingers to this day.
